founders.bio: Prior to founding Edge Zero, Richard McIndoe served as the CEO of EnergyAustralia from 2006 to 2014, where he grew the business from a single power station into a national utility with over $8 billion in assets. His extensive leadership experience includes tenure as the Managing Director of CLP Power Asia (China Light and Power) and serving as Chairman of both the Clean Energy Council and the Energy Supply Association of Australia. He founded Edge Zero to provide real-time monitoring and control solutions for low voltage electricity grids, leveraging his deep expertise in the Asia-Pacific energy transition.
education: Master of Business Administration (MBA), INSEAD
Bachelor of Arts (BA), University of Cambridge

founders.name: Neal Stewart
founders.bio: Founder of Edge Zero Pty Limited.

founders.name: Arman Ghasaei
founders.bio: Before founding EdgeTunePower in 2021, Dr. Arman Ghasaei spent over a decade in advanced academic research and power systems engineering. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Toronto within the Walter Wonham Lab, where he specialized in the modeling, analysis, and control of microgrid-based distribution networks. His pre-founding career was defined by high-level research in digital twinning and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation, for which he received prestigious honors including the Ontario Graduate Scholarship and the Queen Elizabeth II Graduate Scholarship in Science & Technology. This deep technical foundation in real-time power management and renewable energy integration served as the direct catalyst for the commercialization of his company's ultra-fast grid management technology.
education: Ph.D. in Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Toronto (2020)
M.Sc. in Electrical Engineering, Iran University of Science and Technology (2014)
B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering, Isfahan University of Technology (2011)

founders.name: Ben Hilborn
founders.bio: Ben Hilborn is an electrical engineer and serial entrepreneur with a background in consumer electronics, industrial sensing, and medical technology. Before founding Elastic Energy, he launched the Obvious platform, a SaaS product orchestration tool that scaled to hundreds of thousands of devices worldwide, and held product engineering roles at 4iiii Innovations where he brought the Hawkiiii product to market. He has also served as an advisor for Thin Air Labs' venture capital funding strategy and is a vocal advocate for diversifying the Alberta tech ecosystem into IoT and AI.
education: B.Sc. Electrical Engineering, University of Calgary

founders.name: Keiver Tremblay
founders.bio: Keiver Tremblay has nearly twenty years of experience designing systems at the intersection of energy infrastructure, technology, and strategic operations. Prior to founding and leading operations at Elastic Energy, he served as a strategic advisor at ICBC and was a founding employee at Symend, where he developed corporate strategy and executive operations. His career also includes foundational brand design at Thin Air Labs and operational roles at high-growth tech companies such as Tesla and Apple. Keiver is a multidisciplinary builder who specializes in helping founders navigate complex challenges in fields ranging from quantum physics to civic technology.
education: Bachelor of Arts in Multidisciplinary Studies, Communications & Culture (University of Calgary)

founders.name: Amir Cohen
founders.bio: Founder of Electrical Grid Monitoring.

founders.name: Nathan Hugi
founders.bio: Nathan Hugi is a co-founder and the Chief Projects Officer of Electrical Grid Monitoring (EGM), where he applies decades of utility industry expertise to modernize power grid infrastructure. Before co-founding EGM, he spent over 30 years at the Israel Electric Corporation (IEC), rising to the position of Head of the Engineering and Planning Department. His deep technical background in grid management was instrumental in developing the Meta-Alert sensing and analytics platform. He founded EGM alongside fellow IEC veterans Amir Cohen and Rafi Ouliel to transform legacy static grids into digitized, adaptive networks.
education: B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering

founders.name: Jeff Coleman
founders.bio: Jeff Coleman has spent over two decades leveraging technology and grassroots organizing to drive climate and social impact. He began his career at Earthjustice in the early 2000s, where he worked on a landmark international climate case, and later served as a key strategist for Barack Obama’s 2008 and 2012 presidential campaigns. Before founding Eli Technologies, Coleman was the Vice President of Outreach at GRID Alternatives for seven years and held leadership roles at various mission-driven startups, including Farmigo and Amicus.
education: Geographic Information Systems (GIS), San Francisco State University

founders.name: Adrian Del Balso
founders.bio: Adrian Del Balso is a serial entrepreneur and product leader with over a decade of experience building technology for social impact. Prior to co-founding Eli Technologies, he served as the CEO of Little Universe, an innovation shop focused on progressive causes, and co-founded the texting engagement platform Strive Digital. His earlier career includes key design and product leadership roles at Pilotworks, Farmigo, and Amicus, as well as founding the non-profit Create No Borders. Adrian's work has consistently focused on simplifying complex systems, from supporter engagement to the clean energy transition.
education: BA with First Class Honours in International Development Studies, McGill University
Certificate in Urban Planning, University of California, Berkeley
DEC in Creative Arts, Marianopolis College

founders.name: Eduardo Del Balso
founders.bio: Eduardo Del Balso is a veteran software engineer and serial entrepreneur who began his career bootstrapping a web hosting company in Montreal before managing and eventually selling his family's daycare business. After relocating to San Francisco, he served as an early engineer at ModCloth and spent over six years at LendingHome (now Kiavi), where he built software for underwriting and loan applications. Before co-founding Eli Technologies, he served as the Head of Engineering at Little Universe, leading a significant tech stack overhaul for their clean access platform.
education: Bachelor of Computer Engineering, Concordia University

founders.name: Ted Zalucki
founders.bio: Ted Zalucki is the CEO and co-founder of Engineered Intelligence, Inc., a Calgary-based firm specializing in power infrastructure analytics. Before founding the company in 2020, he spent over a decade as a professional engineer and consultant in the North American transmission and distribution (T&D) sector. He notably served as a consultant at METSCO Energy Solutions, where he honed his expertise in asset management, risk modeling, and regulatory defense for major utilities. His career has focused on bridging the gap between technical grid operations and strategic investment planning through data-driven analytics.
education: University of Toronto (Industrial Engineering)
University of Toronto (Financial Engineering)
University of Toronto (ELITE Certificate in Entrepreneurship, Leadership, Innovation and Technology in Engineering)

founders.name: Chris Rockx
founders.bio: Before co-founding Engineered Intelligence, Chris Rockx spent more than five years as a consultant in the power systems industry, where he specialized in implementing ground-up models for power grid analysis. His experience as a professional grid planner gave him firsthand insight into the limitations of traditional asset management, eventually leading him to develop the ENGIN™ platform. A technical generalist, he combines a deep background in power systems engineering with expertise in software development and financial modeling to deliver data-backed planning solutions for utility providers.
education: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering (Power Systems focus)

founders.name: Alex Kachar
founders.bio: Before co-founding Engineered Intelligence in 2020, Alex Kachar spent over 20 years as a Solutions Architect and technology consultant specializing in Business Intelligence, Analytics, and Data Governance. He developed a deep expertise in designing secure and scalable architectural frameworks while managing high-performance development teams across various industries. As part of the founding team, he previously worked as a grid planner, identifying the critical data gaps and planning challenges that eventually led to the development of the ENGIN™ platform for the utility sector.
education: Bachelor's degree in a technical specialization

founders.name: Manuel Lemos
founders.bio: Manuel Lemos has nearly 20 years of experience in the renewable energy and infrastructure sectors. Before co-founding Enline in 2020, he held high-level leadership positions including Director of Sales and General Manager at Voith Hydro and Director at Mota-Engil. He also served as the CEO of the Hidromarañon hydropower plant in Peru for four years, an experience that significantly influenced his commitment to advancing energy technology. Raised in a family of entrepreneurs, Lemos partnered with Gabriel Pino to develop Enline’s sensorless digital twin technology.
education: Master's degree in Civil Engineering from Universidade do Porto
Postgraduate in Management from Oporto Business School

founders.name: Gabriel Pino
founders.bio: Gabriel is the primary inventor and technical visionary behind Enline's sensorless digital twin technology, which he began developing around 2014. Before co-founding Enline in 2018, he worked extensively in research and engineering, specializing in power system modeling and the digitalization of energy infrastructure. His pre-founding career involved high-level collaborations with the Portuguese research institute INESC TEC and the energy corporation Efacec, where he focused on Advanced Distribution Management Systems (ADMS).
education: University of Porto (Research & Engineering Focus)

founders.name: Jeremy Suard
founders.bio: Before founding Exodigo, Jeremy Suard served for nearly a decade in the IDF's elite Unit 81, where he rose to the rank of Major and acted as an R&D Section Head. Specializing in signal processing and artificial intelligence, he led teams in developing complex algorithm platforms and was awarded the three highest IDF honors for technology and leadership excellence. His pre-founding experience centers on deep-tech innovation and multi-sensor fusion within Israel's most prestigious intelligence and research environments.
education: B.Sc. in Physics (Cum Laude), Hebrew University of Jerusalem
M.Sc. in Computer Science, Hebrew University of Jerusalem

founders.name: Ido Gonen
founders.bio: Before co-founding Exodigo in 2021, Ido Gonen served as an R&D Team Lead and Algorithm Engineer within the Israel Defense Forces' elite technological Unit 81. During his military service, he managed multiple engineering teams focused on complex inter-unit deep-tech projects and was nominated for the prestigious 2020 Israel Defense Prize (Medal of Technology). A graduate of the selective Psagot excellence program, he specialized in real-time signal acquisition and multi-sensor data fusion, technical skills that now drive Exodigo's non-intrusive underground mapping platform.
education: B.Sc. in Software Engineering (Cum Laude), Technion - Israel Institute of Technology
M.Sc. in Computer Science (Cum Laude), Technion - Israel Institute of Technology
Certificate in Corporate Analysis and Valuation, Bar-Ilan University

founders.name: Yogev Shifman
founders.bio: Before co-founding Exodigo, Yogev Shifman served as a distinguished officer and Major in an elite deep-tech unit of the Israeli Intelligence Corps, where he directed multi-national R&D programs for real-time embedded systems. He later transitioned into the private sector at Intel Corporation, focusing on 'Data as a Service' cloud systems, and held a key leadership role at the construction-tech startup Buildots. Shifman leverages a strong technical foundation in software engineering and product management to scale AI-driven infrastructure solutions. He currently serves as the Chief Product Officer at Wand.
education: B.Sc. in Computer Software Engineering, Technion - Israel Institute of Technology
MBA in Entrepreneurship and Technology, Tel Aviv University

founders.name: Carla Pinzón
founders.role: Founder and CEO of Expand Power
founders.bio: Before founding Expand Power, Carla was a Lead Power Electronics Engineer at Sonos and an electrical engineer at several high-growth startups, including Fitbit, Astranis, and Open Water Power. She is currently a Ph.D. candidate at Stanford University specializing in wide-bandgap semiconductors and high-frequency power electronics. Her professional focus on hardware for harsh environments, such as space and the ocean, laid the technical groundwork for her current mission to modernize the electric grid through novel, compact smart transformers.
founders.hometown: Mexico City, Mexico (Born); Parkland, Florida (Grew up)
education: B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering, MIT
M.Eng. in Electrical Engineering & Computer Science, MIT
Ph.D. Candidate in Electrical Engineering, Stanford University

founders.name: Sam Hashemi
founders.bio: Before founding Felt, Sam Hashemi co-founded Remix, a transit-planning platform used by over 500 cities that was acquired by Via for $100M in 2021. His early career included a tenure at NASA as a Product Lead, where he redesigned tools for the International Space Station to run on modern mobile platforms. He also served as a Code for America Fellow, where he developed a high-impact SMS court-notification system to reduce arrest warrants. Hashemi’s professional roots are in design and research, with previous experience at webOS and the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory.
education: MS in Human-Computer Interaction, Carnegie Mellon University
BS in Human-Computer Interaction and Cognitive Science, Carnegie Mellon University

founders.name: Can Duruk
founders.bio: Originally from Turkey, Can Duruk immigrated to the United States to study Computer Science at Carnegie Mellon University before becoming a prominent figure in the Silicon Valley engineering scene. Prior to co-founding Felt in 2020, he served as an early engineer at Uber and held technical roles at Digg and the cloud storage startup Upthere. Outside of his engineering leadership, he is a prolific writer known for his tech-focused newsletter 'Off by One' and his work on the collaborative publication 'Margins.'
education: B.S. in Computer Science, Carnegie Mellon University
MBA, INSEAD

founders.name: Rachel Zack
founders.bio: Before co-founding Felt, Rachel Zack was the Director of Policy at Remix, where she led policy strategy for the urban mobility platform through its $100 million acquisition by Via. She previously launched the Innovative Mobility practice at the engineering firm WSP, where she specialized in transportation planning for autonomous vehicles and congestion pricing. Her background is rooted in public policy and infrastructure, having served as a Rappaport Fellow at the Harvard Kennedy School. Rachel’s career is defined by her focus on mobility justice and empowering planners with collaborative, data-driven tools.
education: Master in Public Policy (MPP), Harvard Kennedy School

founders.name: Dr. Istvan Kereszy
founders.bio: Before founding Fire Neural Network, Dr. Istvan Kereszy was a doctoral researcher at the University of Florida’s International Center for Lightning Research and Testing (ICLRT). His work focused on the energetic radiation and electric fingerprints of lightning strikes, which laid the technical foundation for his startup’s wildfire detection technology. Inspired by a conversation with astrophysics professor Imre Bartos about the limitations of existing wildfire spotting methods, Kereszy applied his expertise in lightning physics and AI signal processing to reduce fire detection times from hours to seconds.
previous_companies: International Center for Lightning Research and Testing (ICLRT)
education: PhD in Physics, University of Florida (2021)
MS in Physics, University of Florida (2020)
Bachelor of Applied Science (BASc), Broward College (2012)

founders.name: Tamas Kereszy
founders.bio: Before co-founding Fire Neural Network (FNN), Tamas Kereszy was a doctoral student at the University of Florida’s Lightning Research Group, where he studied high-energy atmospheric physics and lightning properties. His early career included professional engineering roles as a Technical Engineer at Procter & Gamble and a Mechanical and Operations Engineer at Alchemr. Inspired by the paradox that scientists could detect black hole collisions billions of light-years away but not a fire 20 miles away, he teamed up with his brother and an astrophysics professor to apply advanced signal processing to wildfire detection. He was recently recognized for his work in the 2026 Forbes 30 Under 30 list for Energy & Green Tech.
previous_companies: University of Florida Lightning Research Group
education: Master of Science in Management (MSM), University of Florida
Associate of Arts (A.A.), Broward College
PhD Student (Physics/Lightning Research), University of Florida

founders.name: Caroline Comeau
founders.bio: Before co-founding Fire Neural Network in 2021, Caroline built a diverse professional background spanning corporate finance, business development, and research. She notably completed the Ford Credit Leadership Development Program, where she specialized in commercial lending and corporate finance. Her earlier career included roles as a Portuguese journalist for the AcheiUSA Newspaper and as a laboratory research assistant at the University of Florida College of Medicine, where she contributed to genetic research. She has also demonstrated strong community leadership as the Director of the Great Gainesville Car Show, a major charity fundraiser in North Florida.
previous_companies: University of Florida College of Medicine
education: Master of Business Administration (MBA) - Esade
Bachelor of Science in Economics and Portuguese - University of Florida
Summer Session - University of Oxford

founders.name: Holly Eagleston
founders.bio: Holly Eagleston is a geospatial scientist and remote sensing expert with over 15 years of experience in wildfire modeling and environmental analysis. Before founding Firescape Inc, she served as a Principal Member of the Technical Staff at Sandia National Laboratories and as a Geospatial Biologist for the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. Her research career includes significant fieldwork and modeling projects for the U.S. Geological Survey and the Bureau of Land Management, where she specialized in using LiDAR and satellite imagery to assess ecological impacts. She transitioned into entrepreneurship through the DOE’s Energy I-Corps and the New Mexico Lab-Embedded Entrepreneurship Program (NM LEEP) at Los Alamos National Laboratory.
education: Ph.D. in Geospatial and Environmental Analysis, Virginia Tech (2016)
M.S. in Natural Resource Management, Central Washington University (2011)
B.A. in Biology/Geography, Mount Holyoke College (2008)

founders.name: Forest Danford
founders.bio: Before co-founding Firescape Inc., Forest Danford was a computer scientist and research team member at Sandia National Laboratories, where he focused on high-performance computing and satellite imagery analysis. He served as the Principal Investigator for the FireMap project, an AI-driven wildfire risk simulation tool developed through the DOE Energy I-Corps program. His earlier career includes technical research at the University of Arizona, where he worked on biomedical imaging and space domain awareness projects. Danford’s work at the intersection of machine learning and geospatial data provided the foundational technology for Firescape's wildfire resilience platform.
education: BS in Biosystems Engineering, University of Arizona

founders.name: Dr. David Cole
founders.bio: Dr. David Cole is a mechanical and structural engineer who spent much of his early career as a consultant in the mining, agriculture, and energy industries of Northern Australia. In 2013, he founded a commercial drone services company in Townsville after recognizing the potential for unmanned systems to solve complex industrial challenges he observed in the field. He transitioned from services to software in 2018, pivoting his company to launch FlyFreely, a drone management platform where he now focuses on airspace integration and regulatory automation. David is also an active member of international industry bodies such as JARUS and EUROCAE.
education: Bachelor of Mechanical Engineering, James Cook University
Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), James Cook University
Graduate, Australian Institute of Company Directors (GAICD)

founders.name: Dr. Nigel Sim
founders.bio: Before co-founding FlyFreely, Dr. Nigel Sim spent over 15 years in software development and academic research, with a major focus on High Performance Computing (HPC) at James Cook University. During his tenure at JCU, he pioneered the use of cloud and grid computing for large-scale scientific projects and was a key architect of the CoastCOMS (now 3CT) data management and video analytics platform. A dedicated enthusiast of racing drones in his spare time, he combined his deep technical background in complex systems with his passion for aviation to build a scalable drone management solution for enterprises.
education: PhD in Information Technology, James Cook University
Bachelor of Science and Engineering, James Cook University

founders.name: Anthony Quartararo
founders.bio: Anthony Quartararo began his career as a professional geographer, serving as a GIS Manager at URS Corporation and a Government GIS Lead at Avineon, Inc. before founding Spatial Networks, Inc. (SNI) in 2000. Under his leadership, SNI evolved from a competitive intelligence firm into a premier provider of geospatial data for the intelligence community and the Department of Defense. He oversaw the development and commercialization of the mobile data collection platform Fulcrum, which became the company's flagship product. Following the 2019 acquisition of a majority stake in SNI by private equity firms, he transitioned into strategic advisory and investment roles, including Managing Director at Soliloquy Ventures.
education: BA in Geography/GIS, Bloomsburg University of Pennsylvania
Graduate Studies in Geography/GIS, Portland State University

founders.name: Patrick Arnell
founders.bio: Patrick Arnell is a serial entrepreneur and investor who spent over a decade leading Rayton Packaging Inc. as its President and majority owner, where he spearheaded its expansion from Alberta into the United States, Mexico, and Chile. Following the sale of Rayton in 2005, he transitioned into the investment and industrial sectors, serving as Chairman and CEO of Orix Investments and CFO of Rangeland Industrial Service. In 2016, Arnell co-founded FulcrumAir to revolutionize powerline construction through heavy-lift UAS and aerial robotics, leveraging his background in complex industrial operations and manufacturing.
education: Master of Business Administration, University of Saskatchewan

founders.name: Quenton Pongracz
founders.bio: Quenton Pongracz is the founder of Future Grid, established in 2013 to address complex data challenges in modern energy networks. Prior to founding the company, he spent over 15 years as a software engineer and consultant specializing in the utilities, government, and financial sectors. His pre-founding career was heavily focused on working with Distribution Network Service Providers (DNSPs) across Australia, New Zealand, Canada, and the United States, developing an international perspective on grid analytics and low-voltage network challenges.
education: Software Engineering background (Specific institution not cited)

founders.name: Chris Law
founders.bio: Before co-founding Future Grid in 2012, Chris Law spent over two decades in strategic leadership roles across the energy, telecommunications, pay TV, and construction sectors. He originally established Future Grid as a boutique consulting firm before transforming it into a high-scale software company focused on real-time grid visibility. His pre-founding experience in diverse infrastructure industries was instrumental in his mission to solve the 'visibility gap' that utilities face during the renewable energy transition.
education: Inferred: Australian University (details not publicly specified)

founders.name: Jeff MacMillan
founders.bio: Jeff MacMillan began his career as a decorated Combat Systems Engineering Officer in the Canadian Navy, where he specialized in weapons systems, data communications, and electronic warfare. Following his military service, he became a serial entrepreneur, founding the eCommerce platform Charge It Payment Solutions and the cybersecurity firm KeyNexus (originally Dark Matter Labs). After KeyNexus was acquired by StorMagic in 2020, MacMillan served as their Chief Technology Officer before co-founding Green Edge Computing Corp in 2021 to develop sustainable, ruggedized edge-cloud computing solutions.
education: Bachelor of Electrical Engineering, Royal Military College of Canada

founders.name: Rudi Carolsfeld
founders.bio: Before co-founding Green Edge Computing Corp in 2021, Rudi Carolsfeld spent over 25 years in senior executive roles within the industrial networking and energy sectors. He was a key leader at Power Measurement Ltd. and RuggedCom, guiding both through high-growth phases and their subsequent acquisitions by Schneider Electric and Siemens, respectively. Following these exits, he served as the VP of Sales and Chief Customer Advocate at Awesense, focusing on smart grid analytics and revenue assurance. A co-inventor of patented power metering technology, his career has centered on bridging the gap between complex engineering solutions and global market expansion.
education: Bachelor of Electrical Engineering, University of Victoria
Master of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Victoria

founders.name: Chinmoy Saha
founders.bio: Before establishing Green Grid Inc. in 2011, Chinmoy Saha built an extensive career in aerospace and defense, starting as a research engineer for Apparati Inc., a NASA contractor, and a staff widebody aircraft engineer at United Airlines. He later spent four years as a lead mechanical engineer at Altex Technologies, where he managed complex engineering projects for government contracts. His transition into the utility sector was driven by a recognized need for proactive grid threat detection, eventually leading him to serve as an innovation consultant for Pacific Gas and Electric (PG&E).
education: Bachelor of Engineering in Aeronautical Engineering, Panjab University
Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering, Wayne State University
Stanford Executive Program, Stanford University Graduate School of Business

founders.name: Jeff Pickles
founders.bio: Jeff Pickles is a technical founder with over 23 years of experience in leading development efforts for hydrogen fuel cells, solar energy, and remote sensing. Before co-founding Green Grid Inc., he held high-level engineering roles at Linde LLC and gained extensive cross-functional experience through work with industry leaders such as Boeing, NASA, and the US Department of Energy. His pre-founding career focused on the intersection of GIS, utility asset management, and heavy industrial infrastructure, resulting in multiple patents for grid safety and energy storage. Pickles’ work is heavily grounded in hard science and the application of remote sensing for climate resilience.
education: University of Michigan
University of Southern California

founders.name: Tom Anderson
founders.bio: Tom Anderson co-founded Grid Edge in 2016 as a spin-out from Aston University’s Energy and Bioproducts Research Institute (EBRI). Before launching the startup, he served as an energy specialist and researcher at the university, where he met fellow co-founders Jim Scott and Dan Wright. His work focuses on utilizing AI and machine learning to empower commercial building operators to optimize their energy profile and reduce carbon emissions, effectively treating large buildings as 'batteries' for the grid.
previous_companies: Aston University (Energy and Bioproducts Research Institute)
education: Aston University

founders.name: Jim Scott
founders.bio: Jim Scott co-founded Grid Edge in 2017 after meeting his fellow founders at Aston University's European Bioenergy Research Institute (EBRI). He spent his pre-founding career as an energy specialist focusing on cleantech and renewable energy technologies across the generation and municipal sectors. His work is centered on utilizing operations research and machine learning to optimize energy efficiency and decarbonization strategies for commercial and industrial consumers.
education: PhD in Operations Research (Aston University)
MSc in Renewable Energy Engineering

founders.name: Dan Wright
founders.bio: Dr. Daniel Wright is a technical founder who transitioned from academia to entrepreneurship after developing AI-driven energy solutions at Aston University. He previously served as a post-doctoral research fellow at the European Bioenergy Research Institute (EBRI) and a researcher within the Aston Business School. In 2016, he co-founded Grid Edge as a spin-out from the university alongside long-time colleagues to commercialize predictive energy management technology for large-scale building operators.
education: PhD, Aston Business School, Aston University

founders.name: Reinaldo Garcia
founders.role: Founder and Former President & CEO of GE Grid Solutions
founders.bio: Reinaldo Garcia is a veteran executive who spent over 35 years at General Electric (GE), where he most recently served as the founding President and CEO of GE Grid Solutions following the 2015 integration of GE's Digital Energy and Alstom’s Grid businesses. Prior to this, he was the President and CEO of GE Latin America and spent 14 years based in Paris as the President and CEO of GE Healthcare International. Since retiring from GE in 2020, he has shifted to the startup ecosystem, serving as a director for Smart Power Systems and heading the advisory board for Brenmiller Energy.
education: BS in Engineering, Universidad Simón Bolívar
MBA, INSEAD

founders.name: John Lavelle
founders.role: Former CEO of GE Grid Solutions and GE Offshore Wind
founders.bio: John Lavelle is a veteran energy executive who spent nearly 40 years in senior leadership roles at General Electric (GE), where he was instrumental in launching and scaling global power businesses. Before retiring in 2021, he served as the CEO of GE's Offshore Wind unit, leading the development of the Haliade-X, the world's most powerful offshore wind turbine. His career at GE included serving as the President and CEO of GE Grid Solutions and overseeing a $75 billion project portfolio as Vice President of Global Projects Operation. A prolific inventor, he holds numerous patents in grid parameter estimation and outage restoration, and previously served as the CEO of Stragure Software Technologies.

founders.name: Saugata Biswas

His professional foundation was built at Washington State University’s Smart Grid Development and Research Investigation Lab (SGDRIL), where his award-winning PhD research focused on synchrophasor-based real-time monitoring and control of power systems.

founders.name: Amit Narayan
founders.bio: Before founding GridCare, Amit Narayan was the founder and CEO of AutoGrid, a leader in AI-driven smart grid software acquired by Schneider Electric in 2022. He previously served as the Director of Smart Grid Research at Stanford University and held executive roles at Magma Design Automation and Berkeley Design Automation. His career began in the semiconductor industry, eventually shifting his focus to utilizing artificial intelligence for climate impact and renewable energy optimization.

B.Tech. in Electrical Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kanpur

founders.name: Ram Rajagopal
founders.bio: Before co-founding GridCare, Ram Rajagopal established himself as a leading academic and serial entrepreneur at the intersection of power systems and data science. He serves as an Associate Professor at Stanford University, where he directs the Stanford Sustainable Systems Lab (S3L) and previously co-founded the ag-tech startup Gaivota, which scaled to over 100 employees. His professional career also includes technical roles as a DSP Research Engineer at National Instruments and a Visiting Research Scientist at IBM Research.

founders.name: Liang Min
founders.bio: Prior to co-founding GridCare in 2024, Dr. Liang Min served as the Managing Director of the Bits & Watts Initiative at Stanford University, where he led multidisciplinary efforts in digital grid transformation. His career is highlighted by a decade at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, where he founded the Energy Delivery Group, and a tenure at the Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI) leading grid operations research. He is a recognized expert in grid reliability and security, holding multiple U.S. patents for phasor measurement unit technologies that have been deployed at major utilities.
previous_companies: California's Energy Systems for the 21st Century (CES-21)

founders.name: Arun Majumdar
founders.bio: Before co-founding GridCare, Arun Majumdar served as the Vice President for Energy at Google and was the founding director of the Advanced Research Projects Agency-Energy (ARPA-E) under the Obama administration. A member of the National Academy of Engineering, his career includes leadership roles at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and professorships at UC Berkeley and Stanford, where he is the inaugural Dean of the Doerr School of Sustainability. His personal journey began in a family that prioritized education after losing everything during the Partition of India, eventually leading him to pioneer breakthroughs in nanoscale thermal engineering and energy policy.
education: PhD in Mechanical Engineering, University of California, Berkeley
MS in Mechanical Engineering, University of California, Berkeley
B.Tech in Mechanical Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Bombay

founders.name: Amin Khodaei
founders.bio: Amin Khodaei is an academic and entrepreneur who previously served as the Department Chair of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Denver. Prior to founding Gridient, he held research and faculty positions at the University of Houston and the Robert W. Galvin Center for Electricity Innovation at the Illinois Institute of Technology. His pre-founding career was defined by managing over $4 million in federal and industry grants and authoring over 200 technical papers focused on grid modernization, artificial intelligence, and quantum computing.
previous_companies: Robert W. Galvin Center for Electricity Innovation
education: PhD in Electrical Engineering, Illinois Institute of Technology
MS in Electrical Engineering, Sharif University of Technology
BS in Electrical Engineering, University of Tehran

founders.name: Kevin Chen
founders.bio: Kevin Chen is the Co-founder and CTO of Gridient, an AI-driven energy management platform. He previously served as a Renewable Engineering Manager at Duke Energy and was the President/CEO of Renesola U.S., where he established their business and project development footprint in the Americas. Earlier in his career, he spearheaded the development of a landmark 250 MW solar program at Southern California Edison and held engineering roles at GE Energy. A licensed Professional Engineer (PE) in California, he has also served as a Principal Investigator for Department of Energy (DOE) research projects.
education: Master of Science in Power Systems, University of Wisconsin-Madison
Bachelor of Science in Power Systems and Its Automation, North China Electric Power University

founders.name: Dalia Patiño-Echeverri
founders.bio: Before co-founding GridSeer, Dalia Patiño-Echeverri built a distinguished academic career as the Gendell Family Associate Professor at Duke University, where she led the GRACE (A Grid that is Risk Aware for Clean Electricity) project funded by ARPA-E. Her lifelong dedication to energy systems was sparked by her childhood in rural Colombia, where she spent months each year on a family farm that lacked electricity for many years. This early exposure to the challenges of energy access drove her to specialize in stochastic modeling and risk analysis for power systems. Prior to GridSeer, she served as an adjunct professor at Carnegie Mellon and a leading researcher at the NSF Center for Climate and Energy Decision Making.
previous_companies: NSF Center for Climate and Energy Decision Making
education: PhD in Engineering and Public Policy, Carnegie Mellon University
MS in Industrial Engineering, University of the Andes
BS in Industrial Engineering, University of the Andes

founders.name: Jesko von Windheim
founders.bio: Before co-founding GridSeer in late 2024, Jesko von Windheim established a prolific career as a serial entrepreneur and executive, serving as the CEO of startups including Tyrata, Zenalux Biomedical, and Nextreme Thermal Solutions. He previously held high-level leadership roles as a Vice President at RTI International and a Vice President and General Manager at JDS Uniphase. A physical chemist by training with eight patents to his name, he also serves as the Lynn Gorguze-Scott Peters Professor of the Practice at Duke University, where he leads the Environmental Innovation and Entrepreneurship program.
education: PhD in Physical Chemistry, University of Guelph
MS in Physical Chemistry, University of Guelph
MBA, UNC Kenan-Flagler Business School
BS in Physics and Chemistry, McMaster University

founders.name: Brendan Banfield
founders.bio: Dr. Brendan Banfield is an electrical engineer and researcher whose interest in renewable energy began while working as an undergraduate engineer for the Canberra-based utility Evoenergy (formerly ActewAGL). During his doctoral studies at the University of Wollongong, he led the 'Desert Rose' project, a student-built smart home that won second place at the 2018 Solar Decathlon Middle East. His experience at the Sustainable Buildings Research Centre and his research into optimizing distributed energy resources (DER) revealed a critical visibility gap in the grid, leading him to launch Gridsight in 2020 to provide AI-powered analytics for utility providers.
education: Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Electrical Engineering, University of Wollongong
Bachelor of Engineering (Electrical), University of Wollongong

founders.name: Kurt Walkom
founders.bio: Before founding Gridsight, Kurt co-founded and served as CEO of the fintech platform Pearler. He began his professional journey at the University of New South Wales (UNSW) as a Co-op scholar, completing multiple internships in mechanical engineering and finance. These early experiences, including a pivotal strategic marketing role at Solvay in France, led him to conclude that business strategy ultimately dictates engineering outcomes, prompting his shift from traditional engineering to the startup ecosystem. He is a serial entrepreneur focused on using data and technology to solve global challenges in finance and renewable energy.
education: Bachelor of Mechanical Engineering (Honours), UNSW Sydney
Bachelor of Commerce (Finance), UNSW Sydney

founders.name: Hugh Chan
founders.role: Co-Founder and Head of Product and Technology
founders.bio: Prior to co-founding Gridsight, Hugh Chan built a diverse technical career spanning medical technology, fintech, and aerospace. He served as a graduate engineer at Cochlear, where he focused on systems engineering and market insights, and worked as a software engineer at the fintech platform Pearler. Chan also demonstrated an early entrepreneurial drive by co-founding the EdTech startup Snack and gain academic experience as a tutor and laboratory demonstrator for software engineering at UNSW. His early professional background includes engineering traineeships at Cingulan Space and course development at CodeCreate.
education: Bachelor of Engineering (Electrical and Electronics Engineering), University of New South Wales
Bachelor of Science (Computer Science), University of New South Wales

founders.name: Matthew Brusnahan
founders.bio: Prior to co-founding Gridtwin, Matthew Brusnahan spent a decade as an expert in energy management and electrification. He served as an International Electrification Expert for the Asian Development Bank in Indonesia and led geospatial electrification planning for Mozambique as a consultant at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Earlier in his career, he held engineering and advisory roles at EnerNOC, Toyota, and SRECTrade, focusing on automated network planning and distributed energy resource (DER) integration.
education: Master of Science in Technology and Policy, Massachusetts Institute of Technology
Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering, University of Michigan
Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering, Georgia Institute of Technology

founders.name: Brian Fitzsimons
founders.bio: Before entering the energy sector, Fitzsimons spent over 25 years as a serial entrepreneur, founding and scaling multiple enterprise software companies in the media, publishing, and financial services industries. In 2009, he founded Qado Energy (later renamed GridUnity) to apply his expertise in data transformation and SaaS innovation to the challenge of grid modernization. He is a recognized expert in automation and data standards, holding three patents in data transformation and frequently serving as a keynote speaker at global industry events.
education: Bachelor of Science in Economics, Fordham University

founders.name: Talieh Zargar
founders.bio: Before co-founding GridWrap, Talieh Zargar spent over a decade building a technical career across the medical device, semiconductor, and consulting sectors. She gained significant entrepreneurial experience as the co-founder of ALD Technical Solutions, a startup that pioneered composite-based wrapping for utility poles and transmission lines. Her professional journey is rooted in advanced engineering and data science, having participated in the CalTestBed accelerator and the Women in Cleantech and Sustainability network.
education: Ph.D. in Engineering Mechanics, University of Arizona
Master of Information and Data Science, UC Berkeley
Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering, UC Berkeley

founders.name: Davoud Zamani
founders.bio: Before co-founding GridWrap, Davoud Zamani served as the Global Business Development Leader for a Dow Chemical joint venture across the US and Europe, where he managed strategic growth in advanced materials. His professional background is rooted in deep technical research, having specialized in chemical engineering and material science during his doctoral studies. This expertise led him to develop patented composite technologies designed to increase the structural integrity and power capacity of aging utility infrastructure without requiring downtime. He previously operated under the banner of ALD Technical Solutions, a precursor to GridWrap, where he began commercializing these proprietary grid-hardening materials.
education: PhD in Chemical Engineering and Material Science, University of Arizona
Master of Science in Nano Polymer Engineering and Composite Materials

founders.name: Hudson Hollister
founders.bio: Hudson Hollister's career began as a securities litigator at Latham & Watkins before he transitioned into regulatory roles as an attorney fellow at the SEC and staff counsel for the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform. During his time in government, he was a key architect of the DATA Act of 2014, aimed at modernizing federal spending transparency through open data standards. Driven by the mission to replace disconnected documents with machine-readable data, he founded the Data Coalition and the Data Foundation. He eventually launched HData to automate regulatory compliance and business intelligence, specifically focusing on the energy and utility sectors.
previous_companies: U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform
education: Bachelor of Arts in Mass Communication and Political Science, University of St. Francis
Juris Doctor (JD), Northwestern University Pritzker School of Law

founders.name: Yuval Lubowich
founders.bio: A seasoned technologist with over 30 years of experience, Yuval began teaching himself to code at age eight on an Atari 800XL. Before co-founding HData, he was a serial entrepreneur who founded AutoDo-It and served as VP of Product Development at Contact At Once!, where he led its integration into LivePerson following a successful exit. HData marks his sixth startup, where he applies his deep expertise in distributed computing and AI to modernize energy regulatory intelligence.
education: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Reichman University (IDC Herzliya)
Master of Science in Computer Science, Reichman University (IDC Herzliya)

founders.name: Selina Tobaccowala
founders.bio: Selina Tobaccowala is a seasoned technologist who co-founded the online invitation pioneer Evite while still a student at Stanford, eventually leading its engineering team through an acquisition by Ticketmaster. She later spent over five years as the President and CTO of SurveyMonkey, where she scaled the platform to handle 16 million surveys per day and led its global expansion into 17 languages. Before founding HomeBoost, she launched the live fitness app Gixo, which was acquired by Openfit, where she subsequently served as Chief Digital Officer. Her career is marked by a transition from scaling massive consumer software platforms to solving real-world climate challenges through residential energy efficiency.
education: BS in Computer Science, Stanford University

founders.name: Adam Sussman

founders.name: Denny Denker
founders.bio: Denny Denker is a technical founder with a background in applied mathematics and data science. Before co-founding HomeBoost in 2023, he spent over six years as a key scientific lead at Brava, a Silicon Valley IoT startup that developed high-tech smart ovens. He holds a PhD in Applied Mathematics from Arizona State University, where his doctoral research focused on high-order sparsity methods for imaging and partial differential equations. At HomeBoost, he leads the development of AI-driven home energy assessment tools that utilize thermal imaging and signal processing to identify residential energy waste.
education: PhD in Applied Mathematics, Arizona State University (2016)

founders.name: Rafal Modrzewski
founders.bio: Before founding ICEYE, Rafal Modrzewski was a researcher at the VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, where he focused on RFID and wireless sensor networks. While pursuing his studies at Aalto University, he gained critical space-sector experience leading the on-board data handling team for Aalto-1, Finland’s first nanosatellite project. He also co-founded the Multimedia Technologies Science Group at Warsaw University of Technology during his undergraduate years. His pivot to Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) technology began as a university project aimed at monitoring Arctic icebergs for the shipping industry.
previous_companies: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland
education: Master's in Radio Science and Engineering, Aalto University
Electronics and Information Technology, Warsaw University of Technology

founders.name: Pekka Laurila
founders.bio: Pekka Laurila's path to space technology began in 2010 as an engineering student at Aalto University, where he joined the Aalto-1 nanosatellite project, Finland's first satellite mission. Before co-founding ICEYE, he demonstrated early entrepreneurial talent by running a media company that produced instructional and commercial materials for technical research centers and hospitals. In 2014, he teamed up with Rafal Modrzewski to spin ICEYE out of the Aalto University Nanosatellite Program, aiming to miniaturize synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) technology. As the company’s former CFO and current CSO, he has been instrumental in raising over $500M in funding and establishing the world's largest SAR satellite constellation.

founders.name: Prashant Dangash
founders.bio: Prashant Dangash is a veteran technologist with over two decades of experience in enterprise IT and global engineering management. Before founding Impresa.ai, he co-founded Abjayon, a global leader in Oracle Utilities implementations, and served as the Vice President of Information Technology at Avance Care. His foundational career includes 16 years at Oracle, where he was instrumental in developing energy and water sector products and establishing the company's India Development and Delivery Centers. His work historically focuses on transforming legacy utility systems into modern, AI-driven, and scalable software architectures.
education: Bachelor of Engineering, University of Pune
Master of Business Administration, California State University

founders.name: Rohit Pareek
founders.bio: Before co-founding Impresa.ai, Rohit Pareek spent nearly a decade at Oracle as a Senior Director of Product Development for the Utilities Global Business Unit (UGBU), where he led initiatives in grid modernization and smart metering. He later served as the Executive Vice President of Strategy and Consulting at Abjayon Inc., a firm established by former Oracle leaders to drive digital transformation in the energy sector. Pareek is a recognized expert in applying machine learning and generative AI to utility operations, frequently advising government agencies across the U.S. and Asia on grid intelligence and regulatory oversight.
education: MBA
Bachelor of Engineering

founders.name: Nigel Barry
founders.bio: Nigel's career was forged by the 1983 Ash Wednesday fires, which struck his family's farm in Victoria when he was 17. Following this tragedy, he was recruited into the State Electricity Commission of Victoria (SECV), where he spent a decade learning utility operations and eventually serving as Bushfire Mitigation Manager. In the mid-1990s, he co-founded Vemco, an integrated vegetation management firm he scaled over 20 years before selling it in 2014. He founded Intelfuse to digitize the industry, utilizing LiDAR-based technology and 3D data analytics to prevent wildfires and optimize utility risk management.

founders.name: Stacie Grassan
founders.bio: Before co-founding Intelfuse, Stacie Grassan (formerly Grassano) was a graduate researcher at the University of Vermont, where she co-invented a 'whey-based fungal micro-factory' to combat invasive forest pests, a project that led to a provisional patent. She later transitioned into the utility risk management sector, working with URMC Asia Pacific on geospatial and LiDAR-based vegetation management solutions. With over 15 years of experience, she has served as a Project Director for large-scale remote sensing and electricity transmission projects across North America and the Asia-Pacific region.
previous_companies: Utility Risk Management Corporation (URMC) Asia Pacific

founders.name: Jeff Filip

He played a pivotal role in implementing regional bushfire policy in Australia and held senior positions at the Utility Services Group and the Utility Risk Management Corporation (URMC) Asia Pacific. His career has been defined by his work in LiDAR automation and the development of 3D imaging solutions to mitigate infrastructure risks. This extensive background in electrical engineering and asset management served as the catalyst for launching Intelfuse's data-driven critical infrastructure platform.
previous_companies: Utility Risk Management Corporation (URMC) Asia Pacific
education: Associate Diploma in Electrical Engineering
Master's Degree in Business Management
MBA in Entrepreneurship

founders.name: Matthew Williams
founders.bio: Before founding IONATE, Matthew Williams spent over a decade as a systems design and control systems engineer, beginning his career at the Australian water utility SunWater and later serving as Managing Director at Exigen Pty Ltd. In 2015, he founded Faraday Grid in Scotland, a high-profile energy startup that raised over $30 million—including investment from WeWork's Adam Neumann—before its eventual dissolution. Williams' work has consistently focused on addressing the 'technological disconnect' between legacy power grids and the requirements of a renewable energy transition. Driven by these insights, he launched IONATE in 2019 to introduce a new underpinning technology for smart, sustainable electricity grids.
education: Bachelor of Engineering (BEng) in Mechatronics, Robotics, and Automation Engineering, The University of Queensland

founders.name: Robert Ricci
founders.bio: Robert Ricci is a finance and energy industry veteran with over 25 years of experience in structured finance and renewable energy investments. He began his professional career in investment banking at NatWest Markets and Credit Suisse before transitioning into entrepreneurship by founding the retail venture 'The Hub.' Ricci later specialized in clean energy infrastructure, holding senior leadership and investment director roles at firms like Sierra Geothermal Power, Molten Power, and Amp. In 2019, he co-founded IONATE to leverage his extensive commercial background in scaling deep-tech solutions for global power grid modernization.

MBA, Cornell Johnson Graduate School of Management
MBA, Queen's University

founders.name: Luca Mezossy-Dona
founders.bio: Luca Mezossy-Dona is a co-founder of IONATE, where she leads strategic growth and ecosystem building for the company's deep-tech grid solutions. Prior to founding IONATE in 2019, she specialized in science communications and marketing at The Faraday Grid, an energy technology firm. Her early professional career was rooted in academia, serving as a research assistant at the University of St Andrews where she focused on experimental design and data analysis. An Oxford-educated neuroscientist, she combines a rigorous scientific background with commercial strategy to drive the transition toward decentralized, smart energy grids.

MBA

founders.name: Ramtin Motahar
founders.bio: Ramtin Motahar grew up immersed in the commercial real estate and construction industry, which led him to identify deep-seated inefficiencies and 'silos' in how buildings are designed and operated. After working in real estate development offices, he returned to Georgia Tech to earn a Master's in Aerospace Engineering with the specific goal of applying aerospace-grade 'integrated product management methods' to the built environment. He founded Joulea to synthesize these high-tech principles with AI and drone technology to reduce carbon emissions and energy costs for commercial building owners.

BS, Industrial Engineering, Georgia Institute of Technology
BS, Economics, Georgia Institute of Technology

founders.name: João Marcelo Von Zuben

founders.bio: João Marcelo Von Zuben is a technical founder who spent over a decade in senior engineering roles at global technology firms before launching KASCO AI (Kasco PD) as a UNICAMP spin-off in 2015. He previously served as a Senior Developer at IBM do Brasil and a developer at Motorola, where he focused on radio frequency and global services. His pre-founding career also includes international experience as a web developer in Canada and a development management role at Global Hitss, providing him with a blend of deep technical expertise and corporate leadership.

founders.name: Diogo Gará Caetano
founders.bio: Diogo Gará Caetano is a technical founder who spent over a decade as a researcher at the State University of Campinas (UNICAMP) before spinning out his company, Kasco P&D (KASCO AI). During his tenure at UNICAMP’s Laboratory of Visual Communications (LCV), he spearheaded high-impact projects in digital TV and autonomous computing, eventually earning a PhD in Electrical and Computer Engineering. His work has been recognized with the 'Inventores' award for licensing innovative AI-driven inspection technologies to the energy market, where he applies deep learning to automate power grid maintenance and pattern recognition.
education: PhD in Electrical and Computer Engineering, State University of Campinas (UNICAMP)
MSc in Electrical and Computer Engineering, State University of Campinas (UNICAMP)

founders.name: Eduardo Luis Carrara
founders.bio: Eduardo Luis Carrara is a technical founder and researcher with a deep background in electrical engineering and industrial informatics. Before co-founding Kasco AI as a spin-off from the University of Campinas (UNICAMP), he spent over a decade working across IT, software modeling, and automation systems. His pre-founding career was characterized by research supported by FAPESP and practical experience in electrical maintenance, providing the industrial foundation for his work in computer vision. He currently leads the development of AI-driven safety systems designed to prevent accidents in high-risk environments like electricity maintenance.

founders.name: Aram Shumavon

Prior to founding Kevala, he established the non-profit Distributed Energy Consumer Advocates (DECA) and served as a Principal at Kevalin Associates, providing strategic services for distributed energy resources. His career is defined by over 25 years of experience as an energy market economist focused on the technical and regulatory evolution of the electric grid.

founders.name: Vikas Bansal
founders.bio: Vikas Bansal is the co-founder and CTO of KloudGin, with over 30 years of experience in enterprise software and cloud applications. Prior to founding KloudGin, he was a Senior Director of Applications at Oracle and the co-founder of Frontline Consulting Services (FCS), which he grew to $40M+ in revenue and over 500 employees before its acquisition by TEKsystems in 2011. He also holds a professional background at Larsen & Toubro (L&T) and specializes in building AI-native platforms for field service, asset management, and supply chain operations.

founders.name: Michael Beiro
founders.bio: Michael Beiro developed a passion for robotics and invention early in life, competing in the FIRST Robotics Competition during high school. While completing his Mechanical Engineering degree at Virginia Commonwealth University (VCU), he collaborated with Dominion Energy on a senior-year independent research project focused on power line monitoring. This academic work resulted in a patent and the technical prototype that served as the foundation for Linebird. Beiro transitioned directly from his university research to founding the company in 2018, partnering with UAS industry experts to commercialize drone-based contact solutions for the energy sector.

founders.name: Lee Corbin
founders.bio: Lee Corbin has over 25 years of experience in utility operations, having begun his career as an aerial transmission and helicopter lineman. Before founding Linebird, he served as an underground utility supervisor and managed drone fleets for high-voltage power line inspections. He eventually transitioned into UAS technology and thermography, where he co-invented Linebird's core contact-testing technology to improve the safety and efficiency of live-line maintenance.

founders.name: David A. Homfray
founders.bio: David's career in high-technology development began at the University of Oxford as a technician in brain imaging before he spent nearly two decades at the United Kingdom Atomic Energy Authority (UKAEA). During his tenure in fusion research, he served as the Engineer in Charge of JET, the world's most powerful fusion experiment, and was a primary architect of the £220 million STEP program aimed at commercializing fusion power. He also contributed to space research at the Satellite Applications Catapult, focusing on technical structures for future energy systems. David is a veteran of the energy sector who has transitioned his expertise in complex engineering to the private sector through leadership roles in solar power and robotics.

He was the co-founder of RVA Aerial LLC, where he led technical drone projects including photogrammetric structural mapping, thermographic inspections, and utility storm response. His background also includes significant professional experience as a designer in the renewable energy sector. Coble's expertise in UAS regulations and technical drone applications was instrumental in developing Linebird's first prototypes and payload systems.

founders.name: David Schul
founders.bio: Before co-founding Linebird, David Schul spent over five years as a co-founder of RVA Aerial LLC, a drone service company specializing in technical UAS operations such as photogrammetric mapping and thermographic inspections. He is a veteran of the renewables and environmental consulting sectors, where he worked as a designer for renewable systems. In 2019, he joined Michael Beiro and Chase Coble to transition Linebird’s core technology from independent research into the commercial Osprey Nonconductive Payload System, serving as one of the primary pilots and prototype builders.

founders.name: Hudson Gilmer
founders.bio: Hudson Gilmer began his career in the telecom industry at AT&T, where he developed expert systems to optimize data networks during the internet's early disruption. Seeking to replicate this technological transformation in the power sector, he transitioned to energy by earning an MBA from MIT Sloan and subsequently joined the demand-response leader EnerNOC as Head of Marketing prior to its IPO. Before founding LineVision, Gilmer served as VP of Commercial Markets at Genscape, where he led the team that incubated the non-contact sensor technology that would eventually be spun out as LineVision in 2018.
education: MBA, MIT Sloan School of Management
BA (Honors) in Economics and Computer Science, University of Toronto

founders.name: Jonathan Marmillo
founders.bio: Before co-founding LineVision in 2018, Jonathan Marmillo spent nearly a decade at General Electric (GE) in various sales and commercial leadership roles. During his tenure at GE, he focused on helping electric utilities improve grid reliability and efficiency through advanced monitoring and diagnostic technologies. With over 15 years of experience in the electric utility industry, he now leads LineVision's product and regulatory strategy to accelerate the clean energy transition. His expertise lies in Dynamic Line Ratings (DLR) and grid-enhancing technologies designed to optimize existing transmission infrastructure.
education: B.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Lehigh University
M.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Lehigh University

founders.name: Nathan Pinney
founders.bio: Nathan Pinney began his career in fuel production, managing biodiesel plants for several years before transitioning into advanced materials research. Seeking to diversify his clean energy expertise, he attended business school where he pivoted toward utility-scale technologies following an influential internship at a gas company. After completing his PhD, he joined Genscape Inc. as a Senior Research Scientist, leading the development of patented non-contact sensor systems for the grid. In 2018, he co-founded LineVision Inc. to provide utilities with advanced grid monitoring and predictive analytics, currently serving as the company's Chief Scientist.
education: PhD in Materials Science, University of Wisconsin-Madison
MBA, Tuck School of Business at Dartmouth College

founders.name: Dominique Meyer
founders.bio: Dominique Meyer is the Swiss-born co-founder and CEO of Looq AI, which he launched in 2021 to digitize physical infrastructure through advanced 3D capture technology. Prior to founding Looq, he earned a PhD from UC San Diego while developing computer vision systems for autonomous vehicles and robotics at the Contextual Robotics Institute. His experience spans leadership roles such as CTO of the pool safety company CamerEye and computer vision strategist at Spectral AI, alongside consulting for organizations like the ESA. A former National Geographic Young Explorer, Meyer has also led digital documentation expeditions and contributed to disaster recovery efforts following the 2017 Mexico City Earthquake.
education: PhD in Computer Science and Engineering, University of California San Diego
MS in Computer Science, University of California San Diego
BS in Physics, University of California San Diego
Technology MBA Certificate, Rady School of Management

founders.name: Shreyas Niradi
founders.bio: Shreyas Niradi is a computer vision scientist and researcher who co-founded Looq AI in 2021 alongside his long-time research partner and roommate, Dominique Meyer. Prior to founding Looq AI, Niradi was a key researcher at the Cultural Heritage Engineering Initiative (CHEI) within UC San Diego, where he specialized in autonomous inspection and digital twin synthesis for critical infrastructure. His early work focused on foundational vision problems, including 3D reconstruction and semantic understanding, which now powers Looq’s 'digitize-the-built-world' technology.
previous_companies: University of California San Diego (Cultural Heritage Engineering Initiative)
education: BS in Computer Science and Engineering, UC San Diego
MS (Computer Science/Engineering), UC San Diego

founders.name: Medi Naseri
founders.bio: Prior to founding LōD, Medi Naseri was a PhD researcher at Simon Fraser University where he focused on electrical and systems engineering, specifically energy and flexible computing. His journey into decentralized technology began in 2013, famously purchasing his first Bitcoin at a campus ATM in 2014 while overcoming a significant personal health scare. After completing the 'Invention to Innovation' program at SFU’s Beedie School of Business, he launched Lincoin Technologies in 2021 before pivoting his energy optimization expertise to establish LōD’s AI infrastructure platform.
education: PhD in Electrical Engineering, Simon Fraser University
Graduate Certificate in Science and Technology Commercialization, SFU Beedie School of Business

founders.name: Mostafa Shariat
founders.bio: Known as 'The Doctor of all Servers,' Mostafa Shariat is a veteran technical leader specializing in compute infrastructure and distributed systems. Prior to co-founding LōD, he served as the technical co-founder of Lincoin Pool, where he helped build one of North America's leading FPPS Bitcoin mining pools. His work currently focuses on scaling energy-aware AI infrastructure and grid-aware mining solutions, recently leading LōD into the inaugural Google for Startups: AI for Energy accelerator program.
education: Simon Fraser University
University of Tehran

founders.name: Nima Amir
founders.bio: Before co-founding the energy intelligence platform LōD, Nima Amir led an unconventional career path that included roles as a competitive weightlifter and a Persian rug salesman. Following a three-year hiatus after high school spent working and gambling, he enrolled at the British Columbia Institute of Technology (BCIT) to study Operations Management. He eventually leveraged this operational expertise and an interest in hardware electronics to launch LōD, which provides grid-aware energy optimization for Bitcoin mining and high-performance data centers. Nima is currently based in Vancouver, where he leads the company’s strategic operations and energy intelligence initiatives.
education: Diploma in Operations Management, British Columbia Institute of Technology (BCIT)
Bachelor of Commerce in International Business, British Columbia Institute of Technology (BCIT)

founders.name: Mauricio Esguerra
founders.bio: Before co-founding Magment in 2015, Mauricio Esguerra spent over 25 years in senior leadership and technical roles across the magnetics and power electronics industries. He held influential positions at major corporations, including serving as CTO of the Ferrite Division at EPCOS and as a Project Manager at Siemens. His extensive technical background is supported by over 70 published papers and 14 patents in fields like inductive components and LED lighting. Mauricio also operated as an independent technology consultant and board member for global firms like EGLO before launching his startup to revolutionize wireless charging infrastructure.
education: Dipl.-Phys. in Technische Physik, Technical University of Munich
Solid State Physics, The Ohio State University

founders.name: Ralph Lucke
founders.bio: Before co-founding Magment in 2015, Dr. Lucke spent over a decade in leading positions within the technical ceramics industry, most notably at EPCOS AG (formerly Siemens Matsushita Components). At EPCOS, he directed a research group focused on developing high-performance ferrite ceramics for soft-magnetic applications. In 2002, he transitioned into entrepreneurship by founding FIT-Ceramics, a consultancy specializing in advanced ceramic materials and technological solutions. His career is characterized by a deep technical focus on magnetizable materials, which ultimately led to the development of Magment’s patented magnetizable concrete technology.
education: PhD in Ceramic Engineering, Technical University Bergakademie Freiberg
MSc (Diplom) in Silicate Engineering, Technical University Bergakademie Freiberg

founders.name: John Acevedo
founders.role: Co-Founder of Magment Americas and CEO of MAGMENT Federal
founders.bio: John Acevedo is a technical founder and veteran with a background in engineering and media. Before co-founding Magment, he served as a Captain in the U.S. Marine Corps and later became a prominent entrepreneur in the veteran space as the CEO and co-owner of VET Tv (Veteran Television). He leverages his military experience and technical training to lead Magment's federal operations and production strategy in the Americas, focusing on magnetizable concrete solutions for electrified infrastructure.
education: Bachelor of Science in Biomedical and Medical Engineering, Vanderbilt University

founders.name: Maximilian Wirth
founders.bio: Before co-founding Magment, Maximilian Wirth developed an extensive background in finance and operations, specifically focusing on sustainable corporate governance within the mobility and automotive sectors. He spent several years as a research assistant at the University of Muenster's Chair of International Accounting, where he completed his PhD while publishing research on sustainability reporting. His early professional career includes experience in private banking and international accounting roles at Ernst & Young in Dusseldorf and the German-Swedish Chamber of Commerce in Stockholm.
education: PhD in Accounting (University of Muenster)
M.Sc. in Business Administration (FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg)
B.Sc. in Business Administration (University of Muenster)
Mechanical Engineering Studies (KIT Karlsruhe)

founders.name: Vishnu Sridhar
founders.bio: Before founding Matter Intelligence, Vishnu Sridhar spent nearly a decade at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, where he served as the final Flight Director for the Opportunity Mars rover and the Lead Engineer for the SuperCam instrument on the Perseverance rover. His interest in space was ignited at age 16 when he launched a homemade weather balloon into the stratosphere to capture images of Earth's curvature. Seeking to bridge the gap between high-end space hardware and commercial markets, he transitioned from NASA to earn an MBA at Harvard Business School before launching his startup. His work has been featured for achieving the first-ever microphone recording on another planet during the Perseverance mission.
education: Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering, Georgia Institute of Technology
Master of Business Administration (MBA), Harvard Business School

founders.name: Nathan Stein
founders.bio: Before co-founding Matter Intelligence, Nathan was a planetary scientist and mission researcher at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, where he led hyperspectral remote sensing efforts for the Mars Perseverance mission. He transitioned into applied artificial intelligence, serving as a technical lead for the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency's (NGA) Project Maven, focusing on algorithmic warfare and computer vision. His professional career also includes a tenure as a Senior Machine Learning Engineer at the defense-tech company Epirus and a stint at a stealth AI startup. Stein's work is defined by a shift from mapping the materials of other planets to building high-resolution sensor infrastructure for monitoring Earth's resources.
education: PhD in Planetary Science, California Institute of Technology (Caltech)
BS in Physics, Washington University in St. Louis

founders.name: Thomas Chrien
founders.bio: Before founding Matter Intelligence in 2023, Thomas Chrien spent over 20 years at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), where he was a pioneer in the field of hyperspectral imaging and served as the instrument manager for the Airborne Visible/Infrared Imaging Spectrometer (AVIRIS). He later transitioned to the private sector, holding senior technical roles at Raytheon and serving as a mission and systems engineer at Millennium Space Systems (a Boeing company), where he developed low-cost electro-optical sensor systems for small satellites. Chrien also spent time as a principal director at The Aerospace Corporation and directed the U.S. Air Force ARTEMIS payload for the TacSat-3 mission. An avid sailor in his personal life, he has spent his career applying advanced optical engineering to solve complex global monitoring challenges.
education: BS in Optical Engineering, University of Rochester
MS in Optical Engineering, University of Rochester
MBA, Pepperdine University
MS in Policy Analysis, Pardee RAND Graduate School

founders.name: Dan Harple
founders.bio: Before focusing on climate data and analytics, Dan Harple was a seminal figure in the development of the commercial internet, co-founding InSoft, where he helped pioneer Voice over IP (VoIP) and streaming media technologies before merging with Netscape. He subsequently founded Context Media, which provided core big data capabilities for Oracle Fusion, and GeoSolutions (GyPSii), a location-based social networking platform. His early career included working on computer networking protocols with the U.S. Department of Defense and roles at AMP Incorporated and Ingersoll-Rand. A 'serial entrepreneur' and inventor, he holds numerous patents for technologies that underpin modern platforms like YouTube, Netflix, and Zoom.
education: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering, University of Rhode Island
Bachelor of Arts in Psychology, University of Rhode Island
Master of Science, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (Sloan Fellow)
Liberal Arts studies, Marlboro College

founders.name: Michael Oshetski
founders.bio: Following his graduation from the Rochester Institute of Technology in 2003, Michael Oshetski spent nearly a decade in the telecommunications industry, transitioning from technical electrical engineering roles into program management. He eventually oversaw large-scale manufacturing and engineering teams, managing tens of millions of dollars in annual sales for various telecom firms. In 2011, he co-founded Micatu after a sunrise conversation at the Hong Kong airport with his colleague Atul Pradhan, aiming to commercialize next-generation optical sensing technology.
education: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering, Rochester Institute of Technology (2003)

founders.name: Atul Pradhan
founders.bio: Dr. Atul Pradhan is a physicist and engineer who co-founded Micatu in 2011 to advance optical sensing technology for the power and industrial sectors. Before founding the company, he gained significant industry recognition as a co-designer of the lens system for Google's Streetview and conducted high-level research at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics. Pradhan's professional history includes years of experience in the telecom industry, where he worked alongside co-founder Michael Oshetski before the pair decided to launch Micatu during a conversation at an airport in Hong Kong.
education: PhD in Physics, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)
SM in Physics, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)

founders.name: Adam Boucher
founders.bio: Adam Boucher is a serial energy tech entrepreneur with over a decade of experience bridging hardware and software to advance distributed energy resources. Before founding Molecule Systems, he established Promise Energy in 2012, where he pioneered solar and battery financing and installations for over 11,000 multifamily housing units. He also served as the CEO of Naak, a company focused on intelligent energy management and load control. His career is marked by a deep expertise in energy system design and software infrastructure, specifically aimed at optimizing the modern grid.
previous_companies: California Solar Energy Industries Association (CALSEIA) - Board Member
education: B.A., University of California, San Diego

founders.name: Shavaj Kallamkote
founders.bio: Shavaj began his career as a young inventor in India, where at age 17 he pioneered a low-cost solar lighting system for impoverished areas before eventually selling the venture. After relocating to Australia, he specialized in computer-based financial modeling and served as the CTO of Immersive, a software development firm serving major clients like Macquarie Group. He is most recognized for co-founding carbonTRACK, an award-winning energy management platform, prior to launching Molecule Systems to further innovate in modern energy solutions.
education: Bachelor of Engineering in Robotics, Bangalore Institute of Technology

founders.name: Asif Khan
founders.bio: Prior to co-founding Molecule Systems, Asif Khan spent over 12 years as a Principal at Klamath Group, where he led direct investments in various operating companies. He also held significant leadership roles as the VP of Operations at Naak and the Director of Channel Strategy and Operations at Hive, a smart home solutions provider. Earlier in his career, he served as an executive at Direct Energy, focusing on the management and scaling of prepaid electricity offerings. His professional history is deeply rooted in scaling energy and smart home technology businesses through operational and financial strategy.
education: MBA, University of Texas at Austin
BA, Vanderbilt University

founders.name: Jonas Villalba
founders.bio: Jonas Villalba is a seasoned technical leader and serial entrepreneur with over 15 years of experience in the clean energy and smart technology sectors. Prior to founding Molecule Systems, he served as the CTO and Co-founder of naak, a Santa Ana-based energy management startup where he pioneered smart home energy solutions through a strategic partnership with the Australian firm carbonTRACK. His extensive background also includes leadership roles as the Vice President of Innovation and Development at Promise Energy and Director of Project Development at Real Goods Solar, focusing on large-scale building electrification and sustainable energy infrastructure.
education: University of California, Davis

founders.name: Natan Barak
