founders.bio: Natan Barak spent over 23 years in the Israel Defense Forces, retiring as a Colonel and the former commander of the Israeli Navy's C4I (Command, Control, Communications, Computers, and Intelligence) branch. In 2003, he co-founded mPrest to leverage his expertise in developing complex 'system of systems' architecture for commercial and defense applications. He is most notably recognized as the lead developer of the command-and-control software for Israel's Iron Dome missile defense system, technology he has since pivoted toward smart grid management and natural disaster forecasting.
education: BSc in Electrical Engineering, Technion – Israel Institute of Technology
MA in Business Administration, Bar-Ilan University
Bnei Akiva Yeshiva (Graduate)

founders.name: Eli Arlazoroff
founders.bio: Eli Arlazoroff is an Israeli software architect and entrepreneur who co-founded mPrest, where he famously lead-developed the command-and-control software for the Iron Dome defense system. He spent over 15 years as a software engineer prior to mPrest, beginning with a significant tenure at the Israeli Navy Computer Center (Mamram) developing mission-critical systems. After his military service, he joined E.R. Vision, working alongside Reuven Gamzon before the duo partnered with Natan Barak to officially launch mPrest in 2003.
education: B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering, Technion - Israel Institute of Technology
M.Sc. in Electrical Engineering and Business Management, Tel-Aviv University

founders.name: Reuven Gamzon
founders.bio: Before co-founding mPrest, Reuven Gamzon served as a Captain in the Israel Air Force, where he managed sophisticated software projects including avionics improvements for F-15 and F-16 combat aircraft. He transitioned into the private sector as a co-founder of E.R. Vision (originally known as WapDwap), a startup focused on mobile content management. Leveraging his extensive background in mission-critical military systems, he helped launch mPrest to develop high-performance monitoring and control software, most notably the 'Iron Dome' system. Gamzon is also a serial entrepreneur who founded Tech4Israel to foster innovation within the Israeli technology ecosystem.
education: B.Sc. in Industrial Engineering, Technion - Israel Institute of Technology
MBA, Tel-Aviv University (Coller School of Management)

founders.name: Kiran Yeddala
founders.bio: Before founding N-Smart, Kiran Yeddala spent over a decade leading technology development at Fortune 500 companies, including Verizon and Time Warner Cable, where he earned 12 approved patents. He previously founded Nivid Technologies, a digital infrastructure transformation company that he scaled to serve large enterprises in over 100 countries. The inspiration for N-Smart was personal; during the COVID-19 pandemic, a severe storm caused a major power outage in his neighborhood, revealing the critical vulnerabilities of aging grid infrastructure and sparking his mission to build more resilient power systems.
education: Bachelor of Technology (BTech), Sri Siddhartha Institute of Technology
Master of Science (MS) in Electrical and Computer Engineering, Cleveland State University
Executive Management Program, The Wharton School

founders.name: Daniel Danilatos
founders.bio: Daniel Danilatos began his career as a software engineer at Google, where he served as the Tech Lead for the world's first web-based real-time collaborative rich text editor. Following his tenure at Google, he held engineering roles at Dropbox and Canva before founding the venture hacking partnership Helix Collective. He launched Neara (originally Power Lines Pro) in 2016 after developing a specialized physics engine to help his wife, an overhead line engineer, solve complex infrastructure modeling and safety challenges.
education: B.S. in Computer Science, University of New South Wales

founders.name: Karamvir Singh
founders.bio: Karamvir Singh is a technical leader with more than 15 years of experience in software engineering and enterprise solution design. Before co-founding Neara, he spent nearly a decade at Westpac in roles including Team Lead Manager and Application Architect, and previously served as a Senior Developer at Macquarie Bank. His entrepreneurial background includes founding and leading S4S Coaching for ten years, as well as holding architecture positions at AutoAnalyst and CSC.
education: Bachelor of Software Engineering, University of New South Wales (UNSW)
Bachelor of Commerce (Management), University of New South Wales (UNSW)

founders.name: Jack Curtis
founders.bio: Before co-founding Neara, Jack Curtis built a robust career in international law, investment banking, and renewable energy. He began as a corporate lawyer at the international firm Allens in New York before transitioning into investment banking at Goldman Sachs. Curtis then spent 12 years at First Solar, where he rose to become the Head of APAC, overseeing the expansion of one of the world's largest solar companies. He eventually returned to Australia to join the founding team of Neara (originally Power Lines Pro) to modernize global infrastructure through physics-enabled 3D modeling.
education: Bachelor of Laws (Honours) - University of Technology Sydney

founders.name: Bert Lutje Berenbroek
founders.bio: Bert Lutje Berenbroek has over 25 years of experience in global sales and account management within the semiconductor and technology sectors. Before founding Net2Grid in 2012, he held executive roles such as VP of Sales EMEA at Ember Corporation and VP of Sales at Ubicom, where he led global teams in the Europe and consumer product segments. His early career included significant roles at Samsung Semiconductor, managing the Philips account, and serving as a Sales Engineer at Cypress. In 2017, he expanded his vision by establishing Net2Grid Hellas in Thessaloniki, Greece, following a collaboration with researchers from the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki.
education: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering, University of Twente

founders.name: Dimitrios Doukas
founders.bio: Before spearheading the expansion of NET2GRID into Greece, Dr. Dimitrios Doukas spent a decade in advanced R&D and academic teaching. He began his professional career at ABB Corporate Research in Sweden, where he focused on renewable energy integration and energy storage systems. Following this, he spent four years as an R&D engineer and manager at the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, leading various international research projects. In 2017, he joined NET2GRID to found its Greek tech hub, scaling the Thessaloniki-based team from just two engineers to over 75 specialized individuals.
education: Ph.D. in Electrical and Computer Engineering, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki
M.Sc. in Sustainable Energy Systems, University of Edinburgh
Dipl. Eng. in Electrical and Computer Engineering, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki

founders.name: Antonios Chrysopoulos
founders.role: Founder of Net2Grid Hellas & Director of Innovation and Technical Growth
founders.bio: Before helping establish NET2GRID Hellas, Antonios Chrysopoulos spent over a decade at the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki as a researcher, teaching assistant, and lecturer specializing in AI and power systems. He coordinated several high-profile research projects, including the European-funded 'Cassandra' platform and the national 'AMNOS' veterinary software. His early career included technical roles at Computer Life SA and the Information Technologies Institute, providing him with a unique blend of academic depth and hands-on software engineering experience that he used to scale Net2Grid's analytics from the ground up.
education: PhD in Electrical and Computer Engineering, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki
Diploma in Electrical and Computer Engineering, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki

founders.name: Dennis Chapman
founders.bio: Dennis Chapman began his career as a 17-year-old apprentice at Tait Electronics, where he simultaneously earned an NZCE in telecoms before completing a Bachelor of Engineering at the University of Canterbury. He rose to the position of senior design engineer at Tait, leading mobile radio telephone design, before leaving to co-found SwichTec Power Systems in 1985. After SwichTec grew into a major exporter and was sold in 1998, he founded Enatel in 2002, specializing in standby power solutions. His long-term commitment to energy R&D led him to establish a technology incubator in 2008 and eventually Nexbe Limited in 2020.
education: NZCE (Telecoms), Christchurch Polytech
Bachelor of Engineering (Electrical), University of Canterbury

founders.name: Alan Chapman
founders.bio: Alan Chapman is a prominent figure in the New Zealand power electronics and energy sector, having served as a director of the Christchurch-based research incubator DARC Technologies since 2008. He is a significant stakeholder in the Chapman family’s legacy of technology innovation, which includes the founding and successful exits of industry leaders SwichTec and Enatel. Prior to launching Nexbe from within the DARC 'skunkworks' incubator in 2020, he was deeply involved in energy research and battery stewardship initiatives across the New Zealand electricity market.
education: University of Canterbury

founders.name: Robert Stuart
founders.role: Founder and Head of Embedded R&D
founders.bio: Rob Stuart has over 25 years of experience in technical research and design, specializing in hardware development and embedded systems within the New Zealand technology sector. Before co-founding Nexbe Limited in 2020, he held key R&D positions at prominent organizations including Fisher & Paykel Healthcare, PDL Industries, and Industrial Research Limited (IRL). His professional history is marked by a focus on power electronics and smart technology, having contributed to innovations in medical devices and industrial automation. At Nexbe, he leads the hardware team in developing advanced smart metering solutions and energy management systems.
education: Bachelor of Engineering (likely from University of Canterbury or University of Auckland)

founders.name: Rune Hogga
founders.role: Director of Power at Bulk Infrastructure (former CEO of NODES)
founders.bio: Rune Hogga has spent over 17 years in the renewable energy and power sectors, notably serving as the founding CEO of NODES, an independent marketplace for grid flexibility. Prior to establishing NODES as a joint venture between Agder Energi and Nord Pool, he held senior management roles at Agder Energi, including Project Director and later CEO of Å Energi Fleksibilitet. His career is characterized by a transition from technical IT and business administration roles into executive leadership within the European energy market, specifically focusing on innovative energy trading and sustainable infrastructure.
education: MBA, ESCP Business School
IT/Business Administration, University of Agder (UiA)
Solstrandprogrammet (Leadership), AFF

founders.name: Hans-Arild Bredesen
founders.role: Founder and Board Member of NODES AS
founders.bio: Hans-Arild Bredesen has been a central figure in the electricity deregulation process since its inception in 1992, starting his career as a technical project manager developing market systems at Nord Pool. He rose through the ranks at Nord Pool to become the Senior Vice President and later the Managing Director of Nord Pool Consulting, where he spearheaded international power market strategies across Europe, Africa, and Asia. In 2012, he established his own firm, Bredesen Consulting, to provide specialized advice on power market design and regulation. In 2017, he co-founded NODES AS, a pioneering independent marketplace for trading local energy flexibility, while continuing to serve as a global consultant for major energy market reforms.
education: BSc in Computer Science, Høgskolen i Østfold

founders.name: Christopher Ricciuti
founders.bio: Christopher Ricciuti is a technical entrepreneur with over 20 years of experience in AI, cybersecurity, and regulatory technology. Before founding Noteworthy AI, he served as the VP of Product at Veritone, overseeing AI software for the energy and government sectors, and was the VP of Financial Services at Proofpoint. He is a serial founder who previously launched and exited eDynamics and Panalytics, both focused on compliance and risk management. His personal motivation for Noteworthy AI stems from a decade spent living in Southern California, where a wildfire sparked by faulty utility equipment nearly reached his home, driving him to develop computer vision solutions for grid safety.
education: BS in Computer Science, Southern Connecticut State University
MBA, Babson F.W. Olin Graduate School of Business

founders.name: Bradley Fox
founders.bio: Before co-founding NuclearN, Bradley Fox spent over a decade at the Palo Verde Nuclear Generating Station, where he evolved from an Inservice Test engineer to a Senior Engineer in Data Science and Machine Learning. A former professional ESports athlete with Major League Gaming, Fox combined his mechanical engineering expertise with a background in bedroom-hardware web development to co-found Palo Verde’s first data science team in 2017. His pioneering work in predictive maintenance and process automation at the plant earned him a Nuclear Energy Institute 'Best of the Best' award and a U.S. patent, ultimately leading him to launch NuclearN to scale AI solutions across the nuclear sector.
education: BS in Materials Science and Engineering, University of Arizona
Masters Certificate in Business Improvement, Auburn University

founders.name: Jerrold Vincent
founders.bio: Jerrold 'JJ' Vincent grew up in Poway, California, where he balanced his early academic pursuits with a passion for surfing and gaming. He graduated from the University of California, Irvine with a degree in Business Economics at just 20 years old before pivoting toward software and data science, eventually leading the industry's first in-house data science team at the Palo Verde Nuclear Generating Station in 2017. Driven by the frustration of administrative inefficiencies in nuclear operations, he and his co-founder developed machine learning tools that earned the 2020 NEI Top Innovative Practice Award, laying the technical foundation for the eventual launch of NuclearN AI.
education: BS in Business Economics, University of California, Irvine
MS in Computer Science, Johns Hopkins University

founders.name: Michel Kohanim
founders.role: Founder of Nucore.ai & CEO of Universal Devices, Inc.
founders.bio: Michel Kohanim is a technical leader and artificial intelligence expert who spent a significant portion of his early career as a veteran at IBM. Before founding Universal Devices in 2007, he specialized in systems engineering, sensors, and machine-to-machine communications. His professional mission is deeply rooted in his personal history of relocating to the U.S. from a region where frequent blackouts were a daily reality, a background that inspired his focus on open energy standards and the 'demand-x' (demand flexibility) sector. Most recently, he launched Nucore.ai as a nonprofit foundation to facilitate innovation in open and interoperable energy platforms.
education: Master's in Artificial Intelligence
Bachelor of Mathematics in Computer Science, University of Waterloo

founders.name: Rolf Bienert
founders.role: Co-Founder of NuCore.ai Foundation & Managing Director of OpenADR Alliance
founders.bio: Rolf Bienert is a standards expert with over 30 years of experience across the telecommunications and smart grid sectors. Originally a telecom engineer focused on wireless protocols like Bluetooth and ZigBee at a global testing firm, he transitioned into energy standards in response to the California energy crisis. He has spent over a decade leading the OpenADR Alliance and recently co-founded the NuCore.ai Foundation to provide the energy industry with license-free, community-driven AI models and local agents.
education: M.S. in Electrical Engineering - Telecommunications, University of Applied Sciences in Saarbrücken, Germany

founders.name: Dave Mor
founders.bio: Before founding OneLayer, Dave Mor served for 15 years in the special operations department of the Israeli Military Intelligence (Aman), where he specialized in cybersecurity and technological R&D within the elite Unit 81. His military career spanned roles as an analyst, team leader, and R&D project manager, focusing on complex cross-domain intelligence and cellular technology projects. Following his service, he transitioned to the private sector as the Chief of Innovative Technologies at SMARTECH, where he led digital transformation and smart manufacturing initiatives for two years. This deep expertise in both cellular security and industrial connectivity ultimately led him to co-found OneLayer in 2021 to address security gaps in private 5G and LTE networks.
education: Bachelor of Science in Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Technion - Israel Institute of Technology

founders.name: Or Turgeman
founders.bio: Prior to co-founding OneLayer in 2021, Or Turgeman spent nearly eight years in the Israeli Military Intelligence's elite Unit 81, where he served as a System Architect and Head of Software R&D. In these roles, he managed a section of 35 software engineers and oversaw the development of complex hardware-software integrated projects and advanced research methods like code reversing. His professional background is deeply rooted in high-level engineering and the architecture of secure, large-scale communication systems developed for national intelligence. He transitioned to the private sector to apply his expertise in cellular network security to the emerging enterprise 5G and LTE markets.
education: Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering, Technion - Israel Institute of Technology
Master of Business Administration, Tel Aviv University - Coller School of Management

founders.name: Indra den Bakker
founders.bio: A deep learning engineer and serial founder, Indra transitioned from high-scale data science in advertising to climate technology after winning a 2017 Kaggle competition for monitoring Amazon deforestation. He served as the first employee and data scientist at Screen6 and later founded 23insights before co-founding Overstory (originally 20tree.ai) to leverage AI and satellite imagery for planetary health. He was a dedicated mentor at Udacity and authored the 'Python Deep Learning Cookbook,' focusing his career on using technical innovation to mitigate the climate and biodiversity crises until his passing in 2024.
education: Business Mathematics and Informatics, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

founders.name: Anniek Schouten
founders.bio: Prior to co-founding Overstory in 2018, Anniek Schouten developed a strong background in organizational strategy and transformation as a consultant at Kirkman Company. Her early professional career included a role as a Junior Consultant at UniPartners Nederland and serving as the Chairman of the student organization Yassassin. She transitioned into climate tech after co-founding 20tree.ai (now Overstory) alongside Indra den Bakker and Roelof Pieters, originally launching the venture in Lisbon after winning a machine learning competition focused on Amazonian deforestation.
education: Master of Science in Business Studies, University of Amsterdam
Bachelor of Science in Arbeids- en organisatiepsychologie, University of Amsterdam

founders.name: Roelof Pieters
founders.bio: Before founding Overstory, Roelof Pieters bridged the gap between social sciences and deep tech, transitioning from development work in Ghana to a PhD candidacy in Theoretical Computer Science at KTH Royal Institute of Technology. He is a serial founder who previously launched Creative.ai, a startup focused on generative AI for creative industries, and Sunshine Lab. Pieters also founded the Stockholm.AI community, establishing himself as a central figure in the European AI ecosystem prior to focusing on climate technology.
education: PhD Candidate, Theoretical Computer Science (KTH Royal Institute of Technology)
MA, Social Anthropology (Leiden University / University of Amsterdam)
Computer Science (University of Amsterdam)

founders.name: Sonia Kastner
founders.bio: Before founding Pano AI, Sonia Kastner spent over a decade in operations and supply chain leadership at mission-driven startups like Nest and Alta Devices. Her career began in the public sector, where she worked in economic development for New York City under Mayor Michael Bloomberg and on political campaigns. A physics major with a passion for hardware, she moved to California in 2007 to join the green energy movement, later leveraging her IoT expertise to tackle wildfire detection.
previous_companies: New York City Economic Development Corporation
education: AB in Physics, Harvard University
MBA, Stanford Graduate School of Business

founders.name: Arvind Satyam
founders.bio: Arvind Satyam is a seasoned technology executive who spent over 15 years at Cisco, where he served as Managing Director for Global Public Sector and led a $13 billion growth initiative focused on critical infrastructure, IoT, and Smart Cities. A native of Sydney, Australia, his professional focus shifted toward climate resilience after witnessing the devastating 'Black Summer' bushfires of 2020. This experience inspired him to co-found Pano AI to leverage computer vision and satellite data for early wildfire detection. Beyond his work at Pano AI, he is a Young Global Leader with the World Economic Forum and an advisor to numerous startups in the sustainability and IoT sectors.
education: Bachelor of Computer Engineering, University of New South Wales
Master of Finance, University of New South Wales
Harvard Business School (Alumnus)
Harvard Kennedy School (Global Leadership Program)
Princeton University

founders.name: Evan Rains
founders.bio: Evan Rains is the co-founder of PaySitters, an automated bill-tracking platform born from his personal experiences with financial instability and a life defined by resilience. His pre-founding history is marked by extreme physical and emotional challenges, including surviving a traumatic brain injury at age 14 and overcoming significant childhood health crises. Before launching PaySitters, Rains worked as a freelancer where he faced the stress of living paycheck-to-paycheck, a journey of 'spiritual metamorphosis' that inspired him to build tools for financial peace of mind.

founders.name: Matthew Stephenson
founders.bio: Founder of Paysitters.

founders.name: Larry J. Stephens
founders.bio: Born in 1941 to sharecropper parents in Pillowville, Tennessee, Larry J. Stephens rose from humble rural beginnings to become a distinguished Professor of Mathematics and Statistics at the University of Nebraska at Omaha. Before co-founding PaySitters, he spent over 40 years teaching and conducting research at prestigious institutions, including NASA, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, and Los Alamos National Laboratory. A prolific author, he has published more than 14 books, notably several volumes in the Schaum's Outlines series on statistics and algebra. His career prior to founding PaySitters was further defined by extensive consulting work for major corporations like 3M, where he conducted advanced seminars for engineering groups.
education: Ph.D. in Statistics, Oklahoma State University
M.A. in Mathematics, University of Arizona
B.S. in Mathematics/Physics, Memphis State University

founders.name: Jim Welsh
founders.bio: Jim Welsh spent over 20 years in the technology sector before co-founding Peak Nano in 2016, including a lengthy tenure at Compaq and Hewlett-Packard where he served as an engineering program manager. In 2010, he transitioned to entrepreneurship by co-founding MW2 Defense, a nanomaterials venture that developed carbon nanotube solutions for the aerospace and defense industries. He later held senior leadership roles at Emulex, where he led a global team to launch disruptive converged networking technologies and forged major strategic partnerships with Dell, IBM, and HP. Born into a military family as the youngest of seven children, Welsh's career is defined by a focus on transitioning advanced research into scalable, real-world commercial products.
education: Bachelor of Science, Texas A&M University
Master of Business Administration, University of Colorado Colorado Springs

founders.name: Chad Lewis
founders.bio: Prior to co-founding Peak Nano in 2016, Chad Lewis held key executive roles at Molecular Rebar Design and its defense-focused spinout, MW2 Defense. With a robust background in investment banking and finance, he has secured over $175 million in equity and development funding for nanotechnology ventures since 2013. Lewis was also instrumental in establishing Black Diamond Structures (BDS), a joint venture with SABIC, where he focused on integrating discrete carbon nanotubes into high-performance battery and military applications.
education: Texas A&M University

founders.name: Tom Nudell
founders.bio: Tom Nudell is an electrical engineer and energy technologist who previously served as the Director of Product and Solutions Analytics at Smart Wires Inc., where he developed analytical frameworks for renewable energy systems. Prior to his work in industry, he was a postdoctoral associate at MIT’s Active Adaptive Control Lab, where he researched transactive energy and smart grid optimization. He was also a founding member of the venture Enrich and conducted extensive doctoral research on integrating renewable resources into the power grid. His career has consistently focused on moving the energy sector away from carbon-based sources through advanced engineering and data-driven models.
education: PhD in Electrical Engineering, North Carolina State University
MS in Electrical Engineering, North Carolina State University
BA in Physics, Kalamazoo College

founders.name: Dionysios Stamatiadis
founders.bio: Before founding PIQ Energy, Dionysios Stamatiadis built an extensive career in power systems engineering, specifically focusing on transmission and distribution coordination. He previously served as an engineer at UK Power Networks and collaborated with the National Grid in the United Kingdom on complex grid management solutions. A recognized expert in his field, he has held leadership roles within CIGRE (International Council on Large Electric Systems) as a Working Group Lead and has been an active contributor to the IEEE Power & Energy Society.
education: National Technical University of Athens

founders.name: Alberto Méndez
founders.bio: Alberto Méndez Rebollo is a seasoned energy executive and entrepreneur who dedicated over two decades to leading major global renewable energy initiatives before co-founding Plexigrid in 2020. He notably served as the Regional CEO for Siemens Gamesa and held various senior leadership roles at Vattenfall, including Head of Wind Power for the Nordic region and Chief Procurement Officer. His extensive experience in the wind and solar sectors led him to recognize power grids as the critical bottleneck in the energy transition. Beyond his corporate career, he is an active investor and board member, currently serving as an independent director for the global EV charging leader XCharge.
education: MSc in Industrial Engineering (Power Systems), University of Oviedo
Executive MBA, CEIBS (China Europe International Business School)

founders.name: Rubén Medina Santos
founders.bio: Rubén Medina Santos is a co-founder of Plexigrid with over a decade of leadership experience in the energy and renewables sector. Before founding Plexigrid in 2020, he served as the Director of Engineering and Construction at OX2, a leading European renewable energy developer. He also held various engineering and project planning roles at Vattenfall, where he focused on onshore wind infrastructure and grid investment planning.
education: Engineering degree, University of Oviedo

founders.name: Pablo Arboleya
founders.bio: Pablo Arboleya is an accomplished academic and engineer who spent nearly two decades in power systems research before co-founding Plexigrid in 2020. A Full Professor at the University of Oviedo, he previously co-founded the LEMUR research group, where he led initiatives in energy management and microgrid modeling. His pre-founding career is marked by international prestige, including visiting professorships at the University of Illinois and the University of British Columbia, as well as serving as the Managing Editor for the International Journal of Electrical Power & Energy Systems.
previous_companies: International Journal of Electrical Power & Energy Systems
education: PhD in Electrical Engineering (with distinction), University of Oviedo (2005)
M.Eng in Electrical Engineering, University of Oviedo (2001)

founders.name: Mohak Mangal
founders.bio: Before founding Pravāh, Mohak Mangal built an extensive career in development economics and investigative media, working as an economist for the World Bank and the International Growth Centre (IGC) in Myanmar. He gained significant field experience at the Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL) in rural Bihar and contributed as a researcher and editor for major outlets like Vox.com and ThePrint. During this period, he also launched 'Soch by Mohak Mangal,' a prominent YouTube channel known for data-driven socio-economic analysis. His transition into the energy sector followed an MBA at Stanford, where he leveraged his economics background to address inefficiencies in the Indian electricity grid.
previous_companies: Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL)
education: Bachelor of Science in Economics, Singapore Management University
Master of Arts in International and Development Economics, Yale University
Master of Business Administration (MBA), Stanford University

founders.name: Dhruv Suri
founders.bio: Dhruv Suri is a climate researcher and engineer who began his professional journey with a degree in aeronautical engineering before pursuing advanced energy research at Stanford. Prior to co-founding Pravāh, he built real-time grid tools at Google X and served as a visiting student researcher at the MIT D-Lab. A serial entrepreneur, he previously co-founded Candela Energy, a last-mile distribution organization for rural villages, and BlueUrbn, a platform focused on urban decarbonization. His early career included conducting energy research across Serbia, Singapore, and the Netherlands to help scale renewable energy technologies.
education: PhD in Energy Resources Engineering, Stanford University
MS in Energy Resources Engineering, Stanford University
BS in Aeronautical Engineering, Manipal Institute of Technology

founders.name: Aman Gupta
founders.bio: Aman Gupta is a co-founder of Pravāh, an AI grid intelligence startup launched on the Stanford campus to modernize electricity forecasting and prevent blackouts. Before founding Pravāh, he served as a Physical Science Research Scientist at the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability and as a postdoctoral scholar at LMU Munich, specializing in atmospheric dynamics. His pre-founding experience includes co-developing climate-foundation models with NASA and IBM and conducting advanced research on stratospheric transport and monsoon dynamics. Aman’s move into the startup world was driven by a personal mission to solve energy reliability issues in India, inspired by the frequent power outages affecting families in the Delhi-NCR region.
education: PhD in Mathematics and Atmosphere-Ocean Science, NYU Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences
B.Tech in Mathematics & Computing, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Guwahati

founders.name: Nick Brown
founders.bio: Nick Brown is a co-founder of Pravāh, an AI-native grid intelligence startup he helped launch while at Stanford University. Along with his co-founders Mohak Mangal, Dhruv Suri, and Aman Gupta, he focuses on modernizing electricity grid forecasting and operations to prevent outages and optimize resource use for utilities. The venture has secured backing from top-tier investors including Khosla Ventures, Pear VC, and Conviction.
education: Stanford University

founders.name: Eran Inbar
founders.bio: Before founding Prisma Photonics in 2017, Eran Inbar was a prominent figure in the fiber laser industry, serving for 15 years as the founder and CEO of V-Gen, which became a dominant global player before being acquired by Newport Corporation. His professional foundation was built during his service in the Israel Defense Forces, where he gained extensive hands-on experience in top intelligence units. A deep-tech specialist with multiple patents in novel laser design, Inbar combines rigorous academic research with over two decades of experience scaling high-tech companies in the sensing and photonics sectors.
education: Ph.D. in Physical Electronics, Tel-Aviv University
B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering, Tel-Aviv University

founders.name: Eitan Rowen
founders.bio: Dr. Eitan Rowen is a co-founder and the CTO of Prisma Photonics, where he leads the development of next-generation fiber-optic sensing solutions for large-scale infrastructure. Before starting the company in 2017, he spent over a decade as the leading researcher at V-Gen (later acquired by Spectra-Physics/Newport), where he specialized in the development of advanced fiber laser systems and pulse shaping technologies. His earlier career was centered in academic research at the Weizmann Institute of Science and Tel Aviv University, focusing on complex physics phenomena such as Bose-Einstein Condensates (BEC) and many-body excitations.
education: PhD in Physics, Weizmann Institute of Science
M.Sc in Physics, Tel Aviv University

founders.name: T.J. Ragsdale
founders.bio: Before founding Raad Labs, T.J. Ragsdale co-founded the Entheos Network, a battery storage DePIN protocol, and served as the Real World Assets (RWA) manager at MakerDAO. At MakerDAO, he was instrumental in bridging traditional financial assets like renewable energy and carbon credits onto the blockchain to diversify the protocol's revenue. He is a prolific writer on the intersection of Web3 and climate tech, often sharing insights through his 'Vulpine View' Substack and articles for Nasdaq. His work centers on utilizing decentralized physical infrastructure networks (DePIN) to solve global environmental data gaps.
education: University of Washington

founders.name: Philip Krim
founders.bio: Philip Krim is a prolific serial entrepreneur who began his career as a marketing student at the University of Texas, where he founded his first e-commerce company, The Merrick Group, out of his dorm room. He later founded and served as CEO of Vocalize Mobile, a mobile advertising platform, before co-founding Casper in 2014 and leading the mattress disruptor to a 2020 IPO. Currently, he serves as the Managing Partner of Montauk Ventures and CEO of Montauk Climate, where he co-founded Raad Labs to leverage blockchain technology for decentralized environmental data networks.
education: Bachelor of Business Administration (B.B.A.) in Marketing, McCombs School of Business, University of Texas at Austin

founders.name: Evan Caron
founders.bio: Evan Caron has spent over two decades in the energy and commodity markets, transitioning from a career in high-stakes electricity trading to climate-tech entrepreneurship. He previously held senior leadership roles as a Managing Director at Mercuria Energy America and a Director at Deutsche Bank, and served as the Head of North American Electricity Trading at TrailStone Group. A prominent figure in the ERCOT market for over ten years, Caron has co-founded several impactful ventures including ClearTrace, Daylight Energy, and HGP Storage, focusing on applying structured finance and blockchain technology to the digital infrastructure of the energy transition.
education: BA in Finance, Binghamton University School of Management

founders.name: Sharo Atmeh
founders.role: Co-founder of Raad and COO of Montauk Climate
founders.bio: Sharo Atmeh is an investment leader and entrepreneur with extensive experience in corporate governance, legal strategy, and climate-tech finance. Prior to co-founding Raad and Montauk Climate in 2024, he spent six years as a Portfolio Manager at Alyeska Investment Group, where he led the firm’s event-driven, climate-tech, and ESG investment strategies. His earlier career includes serving as a Principal at CamberView Partners and an M&A associate at Simpson Thacher & Bartlett, following prestigious clerkships at the SEC and the U.S. District Court.
education: J.D., Harvard Law School
M.P.P., Harvard Kennedy School
B.A. in Political Science, Journalism, and Philosophy, Rutgers University

founders.name: Marc Borrett
founders.bio: Marc Borrett is a serial entrepreneur who previously co-founded and served as CEO of Innovision Research & Technology plc, a UK semiconductor IP company that pioneered Near Field Communication (NFC) technology. Following the acquisition of Innovision by Broadcom in 2010, he founded Reactive Technologies to apply telecom-inspired engineering and signal processing to the challenges of the renewable energy transition. His early career includes roles at HCL Hewlett Packard and Innovations Group, where he worked on diverse tech projects ranging from the world’s first battery charger for ordinary batteries to remote tag technology for Hasbro's Star Wars franchise.
education: BA Honours in Business Studies (1st Class), University of Portsmouth

founders.name: Dr. Heikki Huomo
founders.bio: Dr. Heikki Huomo was a prominent Finnish technology executive and a pioneer in the development of Near Field Communication (NFC). Prior to co-founding Reactive Technologies, he spent over twenty years at Nokia in senior leadership roles, including Vice President of Research and Technology and Director of the Nokia Ventures Organization. He also served as the CTO and Technical Director for Innovision Research & Technology PLC. Huomo was widely recognized for his ability to commercialize cutting-edge academic research, notably leading the Center for Internet Excellence (CIE) at the University of Oulu.
previous_companies: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland
education: PhD (Doctor of Technology), Finnish University
Academic Licentiate Thesis, University of Oulu
M.Sc. in Engineering (Diplomi-insinööri)

founders.name: Kari Autio
founders.bio: Kari Autio is a co-founder of Reactive Technologies Limited, where he has notably served as the Operational Director for the company’s Finnish division. Prior to founding Reactive, he held the position of Technology Director at the Center for Internet Excellence (CIE) at the University of Oulu, a prominent research hub funded by Nokia and Intel. His professional history is deeply rooted in the Oulu technology ecosystem, where he led advanced R&D and digital infrastructure projects, including the EU-funded FI-WARE initiative. Autio is recognized for his ability to translate complex academic research into scalable commercial technologies.
education: M.Sc. in Engineering, University of Oulu

founders.name: Mish Thakker
founders.bio: Before founding Rhizome, Mishal Thadani (commonly referred to as Mish) built an extensive career in energy policy and infrastructure, most notably as the VP of Strategy and Policy at Urbint. A serial entrepreneur, he previously launched District Solar to develop community solar projects in Washington, D.C. His earlier experience includes regulatory and environmental advisory roles at major energy companies such as BP Wind Energy, Pattern Energy, and Direct Energy Solar.
education: B.S. in Civil and Environmental Engineering, Rice University

founders.name: Josh Siler
founders.bio: Josh Siler is a co-founder of Rhizome, a climate-tech company specializing in grid resilience software for electric utilities. Prior to launching Rhizome, he served in significant roles at Opower and Oracle, where he focused on energy efficiency and customer engagement solutions for the power industry. He later transitioned to Uplight, working on platforms that enable utilities to manage customer action and climate risk. A native of Crystal Falls, Michigan, Siler's professional background is rooted in environmental engineering and his experience as a collegiate athlete.
education: B.S., Environmental Engineering, Michigan Technological University

founders.name: Tim Ledford
founders.bio: Before co-founding Safeguard Equipment, Tim Ledford built a technical foundation as an Industrial Engineer at Boeing, where his operational strategies reportedly saved the company over $100,000 per week. Coming from a family of electrical workers, he recognized a critical safety gap in the industry, which led him to develop the Compass safety device as a college project at the University of Idaho. His early career also included internships at Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories and Avista Utilities, providing him with deep insights into the power and utility sectors prior to launching his own venture in 2016.
education: Bachelor of Science in Operations Management, University of Idaho
Ignite Northwest Startup Excelerator

founders.name: Brandon Bledsoe
founders.bio: Brandon Bledsoe co-founded Safeguard Equipment in 2016, a venture that grew out of a senior-year project in an entrepreneurial class at the University of Idaho. Hailing from a family of electrical workers, he was driven to develop safety technology for linemen alongside his fraternity brothers and fellow co-founders. After graduating in 2016, he briefly worked in separate full-time employment and moonlighted as a bartender to support himself while designing the company's first website and refining the business plan. He officially transitioned to Safeguard full-time in early 2017 after the company secured its first round of angel investment.
education: B.S. Operations Management, University of Idaho

founders.name: John Thompson
founders.bio: John Thompson is a co-founder of Safeguard Equipment, where he originally helped conceptualize the company's flagship electrical safety wearable during an entrepreneurial class at the University of Idaho. Before launching the startup in 2016, he gained critical industry exposure through internships at Avista Utilities and Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories (SEL). Thompson's technical background in electrical engineering and his notebook of innovative ideas served as the foundation for the company’s mission to prevent utility worker electrocutions.
education: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering, University of Idaho

founders.name: Ken Falk
founders.bio: Ken Falk is a Danish entrepreneur who began his career in the defense industry after graduating with a computer science degree in 2009. He spent several years at the Danish conglomerate Systematic, where he developed mission-critical software under high-pressure conditions, often working 80-hour weeks. A bet with a friend to start a business within a year prompted him to leave his corporate role and begin building drones in a former tanning salon. This hobby evolved into the drone service provider Heliscope in 2014, which he later pivoted into Scopito to focus on the software-driven management of visual inspection data.
education: Computer Science degree (2009)

founders.name: Mike Hejmej
founders.bio: Before founding Senpilot, Mike Hejmej served as a management consultant at Bain & Company, where he focused on the energy and private equity sectors. He also held a strategy and finance role at Airbnb, specifically working on the launch and scaling of the Airbnb Experiences product. Earlier in his career, he worked in equity derivatives trading at TD and continues to serve as a director for Pierogi House, a family-owned restaurant chain. His background blends deep mathematical analysis with strategic operations across the utility and technology industries.
education: Bachelor of Mathematics (Honours), University of Waterloo
Bachelor of Business Administration (Honours Finance), Wilfrid Laurier University

founders.name: Alex Peats-Bond
founders.bio: Alex Peats-Bond is the CTO and Co-founder of Senpilot, a company specializing in AI-driven intelligence for the utility industry. Prior to founding Senpilot, he was a founding builder at the productivity startup Magical and held senior engineering positions at NVIDIA and Uber, where he specialized in infrastructure and distributed systems. His career has focused on developing mission-critical software and production-grade AI platforms for high-scale environments.
education: Bachelor of Science (BSc) in Computer Science, King's College London

founders.name: James Dean
founders.bio: Before founding Sensat in 2017, James Dean served as a quantitative analyst at Barclays, where the idea for his startup was sparked after flying a toy drone over his parents' house in 2015. His academic background is deeply rooted in earth observation, having specialized in satellite sensing and collaborating with professors from NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. Despite his analytical background, Dean has explicitly identified as a non-technical co-founder who navigated the steep learning curve of building a deep-tech product through trial and error. In January 2025, he stepped down from Sensat to pursue a new venture, cementing his status as a repeat entrepreneur.
education: BSc in Geography from King's College London
Minor in Astrophysics from University of California, Irvine

founders.name: Harry Atkinson
founders.bio: Harry Atkinson co-founded Sensat in 2017 alongside James Dean, famously starting the venture in a London kitchen with a vision to digitize the physical world for major infrastructure projects. Prior to founding Sensat, he held management and client success roles at Fliplet and The Hat Hut, where he developed a focus on bridging technology with real-world customer needs. As Chief Data Officer, he has been instrumental in leading the company's data and customer success teams, transforming Sensat from a pioneering startup into a leader in digital twin technology for the civil infrastructure sector.
education: B.A., American Studies & History, University of Sussex
University of California (Exchange Program)

founders.name: Michael Phillips
founders.bio: A pioneer in conversational AI, Michael Phillips began his career as a research scientist at the MIT Spoken Language Systems Group, where he spent seven years developing early speech recognition systems like VOYAGER. In 1994, he co-founded SpeechWorks, a company that revolutionized automated call centers and eventually went public before being acquired by Nuance Communications. After serving as CTO of Nuance, Phillips co-founded Vlingo in 2006, which developed the technology powering the first voice-based virtual assistants on mobile phones. Leveraging his decades of expertise in machine learning and data science, he founded Sense in 2013 to apply high-resolution data analysis to home energy management.
education: Carnegie Mellon University (Electrical Engineering)
MIT (Research Scientist)

founders.name: Christopher Micali
founders.bio: Before co-founding Sense in 2013, Christopher Micali was a pivotal figure in the early development of mobile voice recognition technology as a software architect and product manager at Vlingo. At Vlingo, he co-developed pioneering voice assistant products for major manufacturers like Samsung and Nokia before the company's acquisition by Nuance Communications. His professional background spans over two decades in engineering and product leadership, including roles at digital agencies and tech startups such as Sapient, Erwin-Penland, and Buildium. Recently, he transitioned from his longtime leadership at Sense to serve as the Chief Technology Officer at Flowhub.
education: Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering, Tufts University

founders.name: Ryan Houlette
founders.bio: Before co-founding Sense in 2013, Ryan Houlette spent over a decade in senior technical roles specializing in artificial intelligence and system architecture. He served as a pivotal Engineering Manager and Service Architect at Vlingo, where he spearheaded mobile client development and service scaling prior to the company's acquisition by Nuance Communications. Earlier in his career, he spent ten years at Stottler Henke Associates as a Lead AI Software Engineer, focusing on player modeling and intelligent behaviors for simulations.
education: B.A. in Computer Science, DePauw University (1992-1996)
M.S. in Computer Science with a specialization in Artificial Intelligence, Stanford University (1996-1998)

founders.name: Fivos Maniatakos
founders.bio: Before founding Sensewaves in 2013, Fivos Maniatakos spent several years in academia and high-level research at IRCAM in Paris, where he specialized in real-time machine improvisation and gesture analysis. A former assistant professor at the University of Pierre and Marie Curie, his early career was rooted in the intersection of artificial intelligence and music technology. He leverages this expertise in time-series analytics to provide AI-driven insights for the modernization of electricity grids and smart city infrastructure.
previous_companies: IRCAM (Institute for Research and Coordination in Acoustics/Music)
UPMC (University of Pierre and Marie Curie)
ILSP (Institute for Language and Speech Processing)
education: PhD in Computer Science, Pierre and Marie Curie University (UPMC)
MSc in Computer Science, Pierre and Marie Curie University (UPMC)
Diploma in Electrical and Computer Engineering, National Technical University of Athens (NTUA)

founders.name: Côme Maestracci
founders.bio: Before co-founding Sensewaves in 2014, Côme Maestracci spent several years as an R&D engineer at IRCAM, where he specialized in the intersection of gesture-based control and digital music. He served as a R&D Project Manager for Da Fact, a subsidiary of Parrot, and worked as a guest researcher at Université Paris 8. His early career as a freelance software and hardware engineer focused on real-time data processing and human-object interaction, which laid the technical groundwork for Sensewaves' focus on IoT and time-series data analytics.
education: M2 in Engineering, ECE. Ecole d'ingénieurs
Marketing/Lean Management, University of California, Irvine
Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Concordia University

founders.name: Tommaso Bianco
founders.bio: Tommaso Bianco is a signal processing specialist with an extensive research background in computer music and real-time data analysis. Before co-founding Sensewaves in 2015, he served as a researcher at IRCAM in Paris and at the Centre for Interdisciplinary Research in Music Media and Technology (CIRMMT) at McGill University, focusing on gesture-based interactive systems. His early career included a 2007 Google Summer of Code fellowship at the Institute of Electronic Music and Acoustics (IEM) in Graz, where he developed open-source libraries for complex data manipulation. At Sensewaves, he applied his expertise in high-frequency sound analysis to industrial time-series data for energy and utility sectors.
previous_companies: Institute of Electronic Music and Acoustics (IEM)
education: PhD in Computer Music, Sorbonne Université (UPMC - Paris 6) / IRCAM
Degree in Electrical Engineering

founders.name: Tero Heinonen
founders.role: Founder and former CEO of Sharper Shape; CEO of Ai4 Technologies
founders.bio: Before founding Sharper Shape in 2013, Tero Heinonen built a deep technical and business foundation in the Finnish software industry, starting at Stonesoft during its IPO and at Tekla. Since 2000, he has transitioned into a serial entrepreneur, co-founding five technology companies including Maventa and Uoma Oy, which both saw successful exits. His expertise lies at the intersection of remote sensing, software technology, and unmanned aerial systems (UAS), specifically pioneering drone-based inspections for the utility industry.
education: Master of Science in Software Technology, Tampere University of Technology

founders.name: Samuel Salmenlinna
founders.bio: Samuel Salmenlinna is a Finnish technology executive and serial entrepreneur who co-founded Sharper Shape to pioneer automated drone-based inspection services for the utility industry. Before launching the startup, he served as a General Manager at Siili Solutions, a prominent software development and design agency, where he led image content production and supported technical research. His professional history includes high-level executive roles such as COO and CFO across various tech ventures, focusing on bridging the gap between software engineering and business growth. Following his success at Sharper Shape, he further expanded his impact on the green tech sector by co-founding Bioreactor, a company dedicated to weather-independent renewable energy solutions.
education: Master of Science in Computer Science and Engineering, Aalto University

founders.name: Joni Sikiö
founders.bio: While Joni Sikiö is frequently associated with Sharper Shape in specific regional contexts, public records primarily identify him as a real estate professional and public notary with OP Koti in Riihimäki, Finland. He has a history in sales and negotiations dating back to at least 2013, coinciding with the year Sharper Shape was incorporated. In the technology and utility sector, he is less visible than primary founder Tero Heinonen, though he is cited as part of the early entrepreneurial ecosystem in the Häme region of Finland.
education: LKV (Licensed Real Estate Broker)
LVV
KiAT

founders.name: Pasi Alve
founders.bio: Founder of Sharper Shape.

founders.name: Justin Lake
founders.bio: Justin Lake is a mobile technology veteran with over 25 years of experience, beginning his career in sales at wireless carriers like GTE (now Verizon) and AT&T Wireless. He later transitioned into hardware and managed services with business development roles at Symbol Technologies and Stratix Corporation. Before evolving his current venture into Skyllful, he served as a leader at Venado Technologies, where he designed the framework for the company's mobile digital adoption platform to solve technology adoption challenges for frontline workers.
education: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration and Information Technology, Amberton University

founders.name: Ralph Hubregsen
founders.bio: Ralph Hubregsen has a prolific background in mobile technology and enterprise software, having founded and exited several companies before co-founding Skyllful in 2019. He previously built and sold Innovative Products and Peripherals (IPPC) to Peak Technologies Group and founded Saillant Consulting Group in 1998. Ralph’s executive experience also includes serving as the Chief Operating Officer of DecisionPoint Systems, a publicly traded mobile software provider, and holding leadership positions at Symplified and MonoSphere.
education: MBA, University of Denver (1988)
BA, Saint Michael's College

founders.name: Anastasios Rousis
founders.bio: Dr. Anastasios Rousis is the CEO and Co-founder of SMPnet, having transitioned from a deep academic background in power systems research to entrepreneurship. Prior to founding the company, he served as a Research Associate at Imperial College London's Energy Futures Lab, where he specialized in microgrid optimization and the integration of renewable energy. He began his career in Greece, earning an MEng from the National Technical University of Athens before moving to the UK for advanced graduate work. Rousis met his co-founder, Dimitrios Tzelepis, while studying for his Master's at the University of Strathclyde, eventually uniting their technical expertise to develop the Omega software suite for smart grid management.
education: PhD in Renewable Energy Systems, Imperial College London
MSc in Wind Energy Systems, University of Strathclyde
MEng in Electrical and Computer Engineering, National Technical University of Athens

founders.name: Dimitris Tzelepis
founders.bio: Dimitris Tzelepis is a power systems expert who transitioned from academia to co-found SMPnet. He previously served as an Assistant Professor and researcher at the University of Strathclyde, specializing in the protection and control of High Voltage MTDC grids. His pre-founding career was defined by deep technical research into grid digitalization and renewable energy integration, which became the foundational technology for SMPnet's software suite.
education: Ph.D. in Protection, Fault Location and Control in MTDC grids - University of Strathclyde
M.Sc. in Wind Energy Systems - University of Strathclyde
B.Eng. in Electrical Engineering - Technological Education Institution of Athens

founders.name: James Wolf
founders.bio: James Wolf is the founder and CEO of Solitude Labs, where he leads the development of decentralized cybersecurity solutions for critical infrastructure. Before founding the company, he gained professional experience at the renewable energy firm Invenergy, the investment bank Centerview Partners, and the cybersecurity company SpiderOak. His background at the intersection of energy and cybersecurity allowed him to identify the critical need for zero-trust systems to protect distributed energy resources (DERs) from emerging threats. Wolf was a graduate student in Applied Data Science at the University of Chicago before choosing to pivot and focus on Solitude Labs full-time.
education: Bachelor of Science in Finance and Statistics, The Wharton School (University of Pennsylvania)
Master's in Applied Data Science (Incomplete), University of Chicago

founders.name: Nikita Volynskiy
founders.bio: Before co-founding Solitude Labs, Nikita was an undergraduate researcher at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC), where he contributed to the Airglow research group focused on atmospheric and space science. He has a professional background as a quantitative researcher ('quant') and has experience leading complex software projects and building embedded systems. His work currently centers on developing decentralized, zero-trust architectures to secure distributed energy resources on the electrical grid.
education: BS in Computer Science, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
MS in Computer Science, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

founders.name: Daniel Kawiecki
founders.bio: Daniel Kawiecki is a co-founder of Solitude Labs who transitioned from advanced academic research to industrial cybersecurity. Prior to founding Solitude Labs, he was a PhD researcher at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in Professor Bill King’s lab, focusing on additively manufactured microfluidics and chemical sensing technology. He also gained critical industry perspective while working at Northrop Grumman, where he researched industrial systems and witnessed the digital transformation of control infrastructure firsthand. Daniel ultimately left his doctoral studies to focus full-time on bridging hardware and cybersecurity for the modern energy grid.
education: BS in Mechanical Engineering, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
PhD Research in Mechanical Engineering, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (Incomplete)

founders.name: Arch Rao
founders.bio: Before founding Span, Arch Rao spent five years at Tesla as the Head of Products for Tesla Energy, where he oversaw the development of the Powerwall and other grid-scale storage solutions. He began his career in clean tech as a founding engineer at Joby Energy and later co-founded Verdigris Technologies, a smart building energy management company. His experience spans mechanical engineering, robotics, and energy infrastructure, moving from academic research at Stanford into leadership roles at major tech and hardware startups.
education: M.S. Mechanical Engineering, Stanford University
B.E. Automotive Engineering, University of Madras

founders.name: Billy Huard
founders.bio: Billy Huard is a former NHL 'enforcer' who played over 600 professional games with teams including the Dallas Stars and Boston Bruins. Following his hockey career, he transitioned into entrepreneurship by co-founding Reliaguard, a wildlife mitigation startup that reached a $10 million valuation before its acquisition by Hubbell in 2019. He is also a published author, documenting his journey from professional sports to business leadership and his personal battles with mental health in his memoir, 'A Purpose Worth Fighting For.'
education: Peterborough Petes (OHL)

founders.name: Charles Murray
founders.bio: Prior to founding Switched Source, Charles Murray spent seven years at Invenergy, where he served as an Electrical Engineering Subject Matter Expert and Manager of Latin America Business Development. During his tenure, he managed the construction and commissioning of over 65 megawatts of energy storage projects and oversaw the development of one of the largest energy storage fleets in North America. He also gained experience as a field applications engineer at Bloom Energy, focusing on power electronics and grid operations. He co-founded Switched Source while completing his MBA at the University of Chicago, aiming to modernize distribution grid hardware to better accommodate renewable energy and electric vehicle adoption.
education: BS in Electrical Engineering, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign
MS in Electrical Engineering, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign
MBA, University of Chicago Booth School of Business

founders.name: Lane Nelson
founders.bio: Before co-founding Switched Source, Lane Nelson spent over a decade in private and institutional financial consulting, notably as a Senior Portfolio Advisor at Merrill Lynch specializing in capital structuring and risk mitigation. He also worked in venture refinement as a Senior New Business Development Associate at Thrivent Financial. Lane has leveraged his financial expertise to mentor early-stage technology companies through the National Science Foundation's I-Corps Program. In 2018, he was recognized on the Forbes 30 Under 30 list in the Energy category for his work in utility power-flow control.
education: Master of Business Administration (MBA), University of Chicago Booth School of Business
Bachelor of Arts in Economic Management, Gustavus Adolphus College

founders.name: Carter Li
founders.bio: Before founding SWTCH Energy in 2016, Carter Li was a Senior Consultant at Deloitte in their Digital Strategy practice, where he led international transformation projects for energy and financial services companies across three continents. A lifelong environmentalist and the son of Chinese immigrants, he holds a PhD in Bioengineering and transitioned from consulting to entrepreneurship to solve the personal frustration of lacking EV charging access in high-density urban housing. He is a prominent figure in Canada's clean tech sector, serving as a founding board member of the Ontario Clean Technology Industry Association.
education: BSc in Biology, McGill University
PhD in Bioengineering, McGill University
MBA, University of Chicago Booth School of Business

founders.name: Laura Bryson
founders.bio: Before co-founding SWTCH Energy, Laura Bryson spent four years as a Project Manager at Solar Ship, a Toronto-based cleantech company specializing in solar-powered electric aircraft. Her professional journey is deeply rooted in climate solutions, beginning at McGill University where she co-founded a Sustainability Research Symposium. In 2016, she helped launch SWTCH, initially envisioning it as a peer-to-peer 'Airbnb for EV chargers' before pivoting the company toward its current focus on B2B energy management for multi-tenant buildings. She transitioned from her role as Product Lead and COO at SWTCH in early 2022 to focus on fleet sustainability at Geotab.
education: Bachelor of Arts and Science in Earth Sciences & Geography, McGill University
Master of Science in Physical Geography, University of Toronto

founders.name: Aishwarya Kansakar
founders.bio: Raised during the civil war in Nepal, Kansakar survived an arson attack at her school and taught herself computing before launching her first startup at age 20 in response to the 2015 Nepal earthquake. Prior to founding Syncrowin, she spent nearly a decade as an AI and automation engineer leading optimization projects for major advanced manufacturing and FMCG firms across Australia and Japan. She has also served as the Chief Operating Officer for Women 4 STEM, where she managed a network of over 300 volunteers to expand STEM education access for tens of thousands of women and girls.
education: Master of Computer Science and AI, University of Melbourne
Master of Management, Melbourne Business School
Executive Certification in Artificial Intelligence, MIT
Bachelor of Business Administration, Ritsumeikan University

founders.name: Jaideep Upadhyay
founders.bio: Before co-founding Syncrowin, Jaideep was a dedicated researcher and innovator with a background in advanced robotics and mechatronics. He conducted research at the University of Melbourne's Department of Mechanical Engineering, where he co-developed 'El Greco,' an affordable 3D-printed humanoid robot. Jaideep's technical foundation began in India, where he led management and technical teams for the Formula SAE chapter at Manipal University Jaipur. A patented inventor and six-time published author, he has leveraged his global technology experience to build AI-powered 'industrial autopilots' for heavy industries.
education: Bachelor of Technology, Manipal University Jaipur
Master of Engineering/Research, University of Melbourne

founders.name: Jean-Luc Julliard
founders.bio: Founder of SYTIS.

founders.name: Guy Julliard
founders.bio: Founder of SYTIS.

founders.name: Joaquin Ramirez
founders.bio: Prior to founding Technosylva Inc. in 2013, Joaquin Ramirez was a prominent wildfire technologist and academic in Spain. He began his career as Director Técnico at Cormo before founding the Spanish consultancy Tecnosylva in 1997 and serving as a professor at the University of Leon for over fifteen years. Throughout the 2000s, he specialized in bridging fire science with operational technology, leading the Leonese Association of ICT companies and co-founding the Pau Costa Foundation. In 2013, he moved to San Diego following research stays at SDSU and UCSD to scale his wildfire modeling software into a global platform.
education: PhD in Remote Sensing and GIS, University of Leon
Executive MBA, ESCP Business School
M.S. in Forestry, University of Lleida
B.S. in Forest Engineering, Polytechnical University of Madrid

founders.name: Joshua Persky
founders.bio: Joshua Persky is a materials scientist and veteran of the fuel cell industry with over 20 years of experience in advanced ceramics and energy systems. Before co-founding Teragen Energy, he served as the CEO and COO of Low Emissions Resources Global and VP of Applied Technology at Utility Global, where he led the development of ceramic reactors for hydrogen generation. His early career included designing high-tech ceramic solutions for turbine blades at Pratt & Whitney and developing fuel cell materials at CoorsTek and Protonex Technology. Persky uniquely balances his engineering expertise with a background in ceramic art and glassblowing, a cross-disciplinary approach that has informed his work on multiple NASA-funded SBIR programs.
education: Bachelor of Science in Ceramic Engineering (Alfred University)
Blueprint Program (The Engine)

founders.name: Vidyut Mohapatra
founders.bio: Founder of Teragen Energy.

founders.name: Nikolaos Trichakis
founders.bio: Before co-founding Teragen Energy, Nikolaos (Nikos) Trichakis served as a faculty member at Harvard Business School and currently holds the position of Professor of Operations Management at the MIT Sloan School of Management. His pre-founding career also includes significant experience in the private sector as a quantitative finance researcher at SunGard APT in London. His research and expertise focus on optimization under uncertainty and data-driven analytics, which he now applies to the development of advanced long-duration energy storage solutions. He is a prominent figure within the MIT Schwarzman College of Computing, where he serves as an Associate Dean.
education: PhD in Operations Research, Massachusetts Institute of Technology
MS in Electrical Engineering, Stanford University
MSc in Communications and Signal Processing, Imperial College London
BS in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki

founders.name: Magnus Akke
founders.bio: Before founding dLaboratory Sweden AB, Magnus Akke spent over a decade as an Associate Professor at the LTH Faculty of Engineering, Lund University, specializing in industrial electrical engineering and automatic control. His professional background includes a significant tenure as a researcher at ABB Corporate Research and ABB Automation Technology Products AB, where he focused on power system protection and fault localization. The inspiration for dLab emerged from a research collaboration with E.ON following the devastating Storm Gudrun in 2005, which prompted Akke to develop more sophisticated distribution network models to detect intermittent earth faults. He officially co-founded the company in 2010 to commercialize his academic research and improve electrical grid reliability.
education: PhD in Automatic Control, Lund University (LTH)
Tech Lic in Automatic Control, Lund University (LTH)

founders.name: Fredrik Akke
founders.bio: Hans Fredrik Akke is a co-founder and the Chief Technology Officer of dLaboratory Sweden AB, which he helped establish in 2010 to commercialize advanced power grid research. Prior to dLab, he spent over 25 years in leadership and product development roles within high-tech industries, most notably serving as a senior executive at the semiconductor firm Switchcore AB from 1999 to 2005. His professional career has been defined by bridging the gap between academic innovation and industrial application, specifically leveraging research from Lund University to develop smart grid solutions. He continues to lead the technical vision for dLab's digital platform, focusing on enhancing grid resilience and fault analysis.
education: MSc in Electrical Engineering, Lund University

founders.name: Lars Wollung
founders.bio: Lars Wollung is a prominent Swedish executive and serial entrepreneur with over three decades of experience across management consulting, IT, and finance. He began his career at McKinsey & Company and Ericsson before launching his first venture, OPM (Operative Management Partners), and later co-founding the major IT consultancy Acando AB. Wollung further established his leadership credentials as the long-term CEO of Intrum Justitia AB and has since become a prolific founder and board chairman, launching dLaboratory Sweden AB to focus on smart grid diagnostics while holding senior advisory roles at EQT Partners.
education: M.Sc. in Computer Science and Engineering, KTH Royal Institute of Technology
B.A. in Economics and Business Administration, Stockholm School of Economics
MBA Finance courses, New York University

founders.name: Jo-Jo Hubbard
founders.bio: Jo-Jo Hubbard began her career in renewable energy asset financing and cleantech venture capital before joining McKinsey & Co as a strategy consultant specializing in digital transformation. During her time at McKinsey, she recognized the potential of blockchain as a coordination technology for the energy transition, which led her to co-found Electron in 2016. A self-described polymath, she initially pursued a path in literature and spent a year in Russia learning the language before pivoting to tackle complex grid infrastructure and flexibility market challenges.
education: BA in English Literature, University of Oxford

founders.name: Paul Ellis
founders.bio: Paul Ellis is a physicist and serial entrepreneur who spent 13 years in investment banking in New York, focusing on debt capital markets and structured derivatives. Following his banking career, he founded the fintech incubator MTL and established CreditTrade, a global electronic trading platform for credit derivatives that was eventually sold to the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE). He also served in the military and held senior leadership positions at GFI Group, running their European and Asian businesses before co-founding Electron to apply blockchain technology to energy markets.
education: Degree in Physics, Imperial College London

founders.name: Nicola Waters
founders.bio: Before joining Electron, Nicola was a prominent figure in the UK renewable energy sector, most notably as the founder of PSH Operations, which grew into the UK's largest solar O&M provider. She previously served as COO at Primrose Solar Management, where she led the delivery and operation of a 250MW solar portfolio, and held operational leadership roles at Push Energy. Her early career was rooted in technical engineering and project development at major firms like SSE plc and AECOM. Nicola transitioned into executive leadership following an Executive MBA, focusing on the digital transformation and scaling of clean energy assets.
education: Executive MBA, London Business School
BEng in Engineering (1st Class), University of Nottingham

founders.name: Knut H. H. Johansen
founders.bio: Before founding eSmart Systems in 2012, Knut H. H. Johansen spent over twenty years at the forefront of energy technology as both a researcher and entrepreneur. He began his career at the Institute for Energy Technology (IFE) in Halden, where he focused on bridging the gap between academic research and commercial IT applications for the global energy industry. A prolific serial founder, he previously established and led companies such as Hand-El Skandinavia and Navita Systems, the latter of which became part of OMX Technology (NASDAQ). He was also the initiating driver behind the Norwegian Centre of Expertise – Smart Energy Markets and co-founded the research and innovation company Smart Innovation Norway in 2003.
education: M.Sc. degree in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

founders.name: Knut E. Gustavsen
founders.bio: Before co-founding eSmart Systems in 2012, Knut E. Gustavsen spent more than 20 years developing and delivering IT solutions to the global energy industry. He was a member of the influential energy technology cluster in Halden, Norway, where he was involved in establishing and operating several pioneering tech firms. His experience spans the evolution of grid technology from early software solutions to modern AI-driven platforms, having previously worked within the group of founders that built and sold companies like Navita Systems to ABB.
education: M.Sc. in Computer Science, University of Bristol (UK)
BI Norwegian Business School

founders.name: Joseph Kao
founders.bio: Before founding Magnefy, Joseph spent over a decade in hardware R&D and management across the chemical and consumer electronics industries. He served as an Engineering Manager at Apple, where he led the materials team for the Vision Pro lens module and worked on battery recycling initiatives, and also held technical leadership roles at Meta and Dow Chemical. His transition to entrepreneurship was driven by a desire to apply his deep material science expertise to global sustainability challenges, particularly the resilience of the aging electrical grid.
education: PhD in Materials Science and Engineering, UC Berkeley
MS in Management, Stanford Graduate School of Business

founders.name: Yutong Zhu
founders.bio: Prior to co-founding Magnefy, Yutong spent over five years at CSIRO, Australia's federal research organization, as an operations manager and engineer specializing in sustainable manufacturing and technology commercialization. During his tenure, he successfully scaled laboratory processes to commercial volumes, notably with Boron Molecular, and authored one utility patent and twelve design patents in chemical processing. He also served as the president of the Australia China Young Professionals Initiative (ACYPI) before pursuing his graduate studies at Stanford.
education: Master of Business Administration (MBA), Stanford Graduate School of Business
MS in Environment and Resources, Stanford University
Master of Chemical Engineering, University of Queensland
Bachelor of Chemical Engineering, University of Queensland

founders.name: Josh Wong
founders.bio: A power systems engineer with over 20 years of experience, Josh Wong founded Toronto Hydro’s smart grid department before serving as Director of Engineering at eCAMION. In 2011, he founded Opus One Solutions, growing it into a top-rated DERMS provider until its acquisition by GE in 2022. Following the acquisition, he led Grid Orchestration at GE Vernova before spinning out ThinkLabs AI to develop physics-informed AI digital twins for grid management.
education: B.A.Sc. in Electrical Engineering, University of Toronto
Masters of Electric Power Engineering, University of Waterloo
Executive Programs, MIT Sloan
Executive Programs, Harvard Business School
Executive Programs, IMD Business School

founders.name: Richi Cleland
founders.bio: Before founding Groundline Engineering in 2004, Richi Cleland spent over a decade working in the electricity transmission sector, beginning his career in the 1990s. He held management-track roles at large engineering firms but grew frustrated with 'old-school' corporate thinking that neglected long-term asset stewardship. In late 2003, while in his early thirties, he and co-founder Ian Flatley quit their stable corporate jobs to launch a two-man consultancy focused on innovative overhead line solutions. Cleland is often described as the 'operations man' of the duo, specializing in field engineering and the execution of complex network construction projects.
education: Transmission Line Engineering (Specific degree not specified)

founders.name: Ian Flatley
founders.bio: Ian Flatley began his career as a civil engineer, spending over a decade in transmission line management and grid asset strategy at large utility firms. In late 2003, while serving as a Senior Lines Engineer at Transpower New Zealand, he and co-founder Richi Cleland left their established corporate management tracks to launch Groundline Engineering in 2004. Flatley's drive to provide independent specialist services eventually led him to invent the 'Thor's Hammer' non-destructive testing technology, which became the foundation for THOR Poletest Limited.
education: Civil Engineering degree

founders.name: Jason Huang
founders.bio: Dr. Jason Huang is a materials scientist and executive with over 30 years of experience in advanced conductors and grid infrastructure. Before founding TS Conductor in 2018, he served as the CEO and CTO of CTC Global, and held senior engineering and management roles at BAE Systems, Owens Corning, and Solvay. His early career included work with NIST on high-profile defense projects such as the F22 and F35 aircraft, focusing on advanced composite materials. He is currently a leading figure in the energy transition, recognized for modernizing global power grids through high-performance materials.
education: PhD in Materials Science and Engineering, The Ohio State University
MBA, The Ohio State University Fisher College of Business
MS in Materials Science and Engineering, UCLA
BS in Ceramic Materials, Hunan University

founders.name: James Huang
